steps.title: BLR ♥️
steps.story: Leaving BLR was bittersweet for both of us. While we CANNOT wait to go on this amazing adventure, BLR had been home for a long time and had so many memories attached that saying bye was a little tough. You can see me ready with a bag twice my size and sidd's bag was too big to fit in this photo :)

steps.title: Uluwatu, Bali 🏄
steps.story:
Finally on our way, cab ride (a long one) was a weird mixture of both of us asking each other how the other is feeling (deep talks) and then quickly switching to questions lile "did you pack your toothbrush?". We were on a 1 am flight and by the time we boarded both of us were quite zonked - it was a 7ish hour flight which felt like 20 hours somehow, the only saving grace was we had a seat empty between us!! Well, saving grace for me cause I squished and fit myself to lie on two seats, while Mr. Long Legs Sidd had to sit and watch me sleep. 
We reached around 10 am and used Grab to take a cab to our hotel. Still zonked - passed out in the cab, reached the hotel and passed out again 😂
Finally, woke up at around 5 pm, feeling slightly more human - we decided to go for a walk and eat. Walk felt good as long as it was downhill, We (read Shreya) would've died going back uphill. 
Ate some nasi goreng at Warung Local, which was a great find - amazing food and cheap as well. 
From there we started our walk towards Padang Padang Beach - which apparently features in Eat Pray Love as well, while we walked, I realized uluwatu is a great vibe - its slightly sunny but not too much, it's hip as you see amazing spots to hang, party, eat and surf but also sort of grounded as you pass small temples with picturesque architecture. 
Padang Padang as the beach itself was good but the entry to it was unexpected - it was a cavelike pathway - the video will do more justice. 
As mentioned above, the uphill climb scared us (read Shreya), so we decided to book Grab bikes back to our hotel. Came back sweaty which made us dip into the nice infinity pool in our hotel.
Decided to rent a bike - sidd saw some foreigners driving around shirtless on a bike and wanted to emulate them :) 
All in all was a very chill day. 
Some musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations throughout the day: While it seems we're living the life by going on this trip - it is okay to also feel a little weird about vacationing for 3+ months. 
Coffees today: 1 :)

steps.title: Ulu Day 2
steps.story:
Ulu day 2 was a struggle against what we call the 'City Itch'! It's basically the urge to fill up your day with too many activities running from here to there, trying to check everything - v touristy, not at all traveller. The theme of this trip is to relax, take it slow - but as soon as we woke up in the morning, Sidd (the planner's) first question was 'Where all do we go, what do we do today?' He even had a list of beaches we had to hit today :p 
After reminding each other that we need to take it slow, we had a nice slow breakfast and then packed to go to Nunggalan Beach. Please witness me with my personal Grab driver - Siddyboy. 
We were very interested to go to this one since we read somewhere that the trek to the beach was amazing. Well it was - going downhill :) 
The trek down to the beach was through a jungle, with lizards and geckos running around to keep you company. We felt like explorers until we met other people coming up and telling us they gave up midway. This prompted, surprisingly, sidd to ask if we wanted to give up as well - funnily I wanted to go all the way (while in my I was dreading the climb back). Once we reached, the view was breathtaking - you could see the almost vacant beach on one side and the hill on the other
The walk felt worth it :) 
But ofcourse the walk back did not feel worth it - and as all treks with sidd and me go - I was crying (please remember that meme with the guy paragliding and regretting it) and sidd kept telling me what a good job I'm doing 😂
Came up and went to Ayu's Food From the Heart - which had one of the best smoothie bowls I've ever had!! People all over Bali are extremely sweet, so that's an added bonus everywhere :) 
After a scrumptious meal, it was nap time, which couldn't go beyond 30min since Sidd couldn't fight his City Itch 🙈
Got up, went to Dreamland Beach - sadly not a good beach IMO. It was too crowded and quite dirty, to a point where we didn't want to get in the water. Caught the sunset and left for Balangan Beach - which had a crazy view point - couldn't trek down to the beach since it was getting dark, but we plan to check it out tomorrow so stay tuned for pics. 
On our way back, we stopped to do one of our favorite things - check out the supermarket 😂. I don't know why but it's a guilty (is it?) pleasure to roam around in the supermarket and check out everything from fruits, to cookies even when we won't buy anything. Ended up buying some local fruits and some nachos and cookies. Guess who picked what? 😁
With hunger on the rise, we ended up at Warung Local again - realised all other places are nearly dead in uluwatu because everyone's at Warung Local. The vibe was great with good music. While we ate, we did another favorite activity (more mine than Sidd's) - eavesdropped on other people's conversations :) 
Musings from other people's conversations and eventually Sidd and Shreya's conversation: Quitting for 4 months and travelling seems like an abberation for us but it seems it's quite normal outside of our bubble. Taking inspiration from Ayu's poster - 'If you're not doing what you like, you're wasting your time'. 
Highlights: Despite the Scooty, Sidd didn't want to roam around shirtless. Its so that the girls don't go crazy, he says. 
Will try to not be such city people tomorrow. 
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Ulu Day 3 - cak cak Kecak
steps.story:
After some hazing the last blog, Sidd agreed to chill today. We woke up and went to this amazing co-working space with a pool! - Lemanja. It was pet friendly, so lots of cute doggos to play with. While I lazed around in the pool and read a book, Sidd appeared to be seriously doing something on his laptop - he refused to come in the pool - girls will go crazy he said 😒
After a relaxed morning, we went to try out a recommended restaurant - The Cashew Tree. Lovely place, great vibe and an amazing salad bowl. Would definitely recommend the Health Salad Bowl if anyone's going there. 
We came back and had little time to get ready before our next activity - which I was very excited for - Kecak Dance Show. It's a tribal dance show which depicts The  Ramayana. The dance is held inside the Uluwatu Temple, which is on a cliff with an amazing view 😍
The temple is rife with monkeys. Very smart monkeys I would say. They snatch random things from you on purpose to prompt you to offer something less valuable in barter. Had a lot of fun watching people offer roll-on deodorants in return for a cap, trying to reason with the monkey, earnestly telling it - "It's a $400 cap!!" 
The dance was amazing, a little crowded - realised the 7pm show would be better - lesser heat. Which brings me to how sidd quit the show midway since his "glutes were hurting". I couldn't stop laughing to even stop him - he left, I watched the show till the end. 
After that, I roamed around the temple - very serene and the view was a bonus. Couldn't help but notice so many similarities between our culture and theirs - For e.g. Donation here is also called Daan Puniya :) 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Not every experience needs to be a shared experience. It's important to do some things for yourself as well. 
Highlight of day: Sidd finally went semi-shirtless on the scooty. I made a compelling argument that girls were not going that crazy also, they will survive :) 
Coffees: 0 :)

steps.title: Nusa Dua
steps.story:
Today marks the start of the luxe part of our 'budget trip'. We took a cab from Uluwatu to Nusa Dua with a really nice driver who was happy to find out we're Indians but continued to crib about how Indians are never on time, "Neva on time ya" he said. Nusa Dua seems like the resort town of Bali. Reminds me of my family trips when 30 of us would go to a resort and never come out :) 
We checked into The Ayodya Resort, Nusa Dua - v luxe, v fancy. After spending 3 days in a tiny Airbnb we were feeling quite overwhelmed here. I think the sight of backpacks was also a first for the resort staff. After some 'welcome bracelets' and 'welcome drinks' - we checked in and explored the property which had a private beach access and a lovely pool. That's all we needed I guess, I don't blame the families for not wanting to leave the resorts. 😂
The beach looked pristine but the waves were deadly - it was impossible to stand still in the water. By the end of 5 min, we were bruised and filled with sand. 
Chilling by the pool was great - but the highlight was cycling along the beautiful promenade along the sea, starting from the resort till Nusa Dharma (which also had a quaint little temple). 
We tried to visit the waterblow (which is like a natural fountain of sea water) but then somebody told us not to go - "The water wasn't blowing hard enough" they said.
Not much to do in Nusa Dua but to chill honestly - Sidd has booked some morning power yoga sessions for the both of us in the resort. I'll mostly be found in Child's pose. :) 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Kuch baat hi nahi ki aaj, Sidd was busy looking for yoga classes with uncle aunties :p 
Coffees: Thinking of getting 1 now.

steps.title: Nusa Dua day 2 🏄‍♀️
steps.story:
Should've taken bets on whether we'll make it to morning yoga or no. We could not :) 
Sidd still woke up earlier and very quaintly read on the balcony while I snoozed. 
Woke up, had some 'room-made' breakfast and decided to go out and check out Tanjung Benoa beach - famous here for water sports. We went there and within 5 mins knew that this wasn't our scene - it was very similar to baga beach in Goa. The soliciting was so crazy, some people came close to Sidd's bike while he was on the road to ask if he wanted to do watersports 😂 
We left, got stuck in mad traffic (with surprisingly no honking or shouting - guess that's island life) to reach a temple that I wanted to visit, realised all temples in this area are not open for the general public - only locals. I got to know that all houses here have a temple within them, so you could easily mistake someone's house for a temple - Like I did :) 
I asked the nice person standing on his door if the 'temple was open' - I don't know how much he understood but he said if you want to see you can go inside, so I went - it was such a lovely house 😍 but it was their house nevertheless! Muttering a mixture of thank you and sorry I walked out to a Sidd shaking his head, asking the heavens "why is she like this".
We got back, waited for the sun to be a little less angry and headed out to the beach to FINALLY do surfing! After 3 days of a lot of indecisiveness ( I'll give my property to whoever guesses who was indecisive here!), we went for surf lessons - my first and Sidd's second and it was by far one of the best experiences I've had as far as water activities are concerned. It was exhilarating - Sidd became a pro towards the end, riding some scary looking waves. I on the other hand could ride a couple of waves for around 5 (6?) seconds - in any case it was too much fun - definitely recommend! 
Too tired from the lesson, we decided to not venture out tonight. Just sat by the beach and watched random fireworks ❤️
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: New experiences always seem scary at first, but you're almost always grateful once you've tried something new. Should keep experimenting - yolo! 
Coffees: 3-4? Couldn't count :)

steps.title: Nusa Dua day 3/4
steps.story:
While we have been up to nothing honestly, on popular demand, I shall update all of our 3-4 followers with our shenanigans 😂
The last two days have been all about taking it slow - long walks along the beach, sitting on a sunbed with a book and dozing off, eating some yum food and trying to picnic like they show in the movies but failing at it. 
Anticipating the fact that we'll be super busy with a lot of activities in the coming days we actively decided to not do anything these 2 days. It's been ultra relaxing just doing nothing, forgetting which day of the week it is and doing zumba with the resort guests (feeling like baby from dirty dancing sans patrick swayze for an instructor) and watching old movies. To keep up with the spirit of a budget trip, Sidd stocked up on diet coke from the supermarket to take it to the beach and pour it in a glass and sip it like a bawse. :) 
The weather has been nice and sunny for the most part which I have loved and Sidd has hated - he has cried and prayed for rain and walked in the sun with an umbrella like a Chinese uncle 😂
Finally, his prayers were answered and it rained, quite heavily - no complaints though, the resort looked really beautiful while it rained. We were able to catch another kecak dance surprisingly at Bali Collection - it's a shopping complex kind of place near the resort which has a great vibe - we randomly ran into the dance happening while we were walking around. Sidd's comment - "free me dekhne ko mil gaya idhar, why did we pay for it earlier?" 😂
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: It takes a lot of unlearning to be able to truly relax, stop planning ahead and take each day as it comes. However, it's something we should all do sometimes. 
Coffees: 5 :)

steps.title: Ubud
steps.story:
We love Ubud. Let's see why ---
The gods really like Sidd, cause it hadn't stopped raining when we woke up today and by the time we reached Ubud - which was a 2 hour drive from Nusa Dua, it was raining, no no, it was pouring! 
I'll be honest, the constant rain was a mood dampener for me and reaching the hostel (In Da Lodge, Ubud) in the rain was a struggle. The hostel's really nice - it has a great entryway, lots of space, cobbled pathways and ponds with fish - will definitely recommend - please book in advance, this place is sold out even during the off seasons. 
We settled in and decided to venture out despite the rain - special shout-out to Anima aunty for giving me this amazing jacket last minute, it has been a savior! 
Once we were out, I didn't feel the rain at all and the moods started lifting. We started walking towards Warung Sweet Orange (a recommended restaurant) and as soon as we stepped out on the streets, we loved the vibe. Despite the rain everyone was out and about, the streets were vibrant with shops, cafes and bookstores. The weather was chilly so you weren't dripping in sweat and the best part - the whole of Ubud's roads are paved with stones on which people have etched messages; this makes walking quite entertaining and wholesome! One of the messages read "Will you marry me - from John" - Sidd thinks I should say yes 😒.
 Walking towards Warung Sweet Orange - the path to it was almost like a jungle walk - across narrow alleys, waterfalls and paddy fields - it was unreal. The place had amazing food, a cat named dog and posters all around. Sidd found some coconut heads that looked like him :)  
We walked back through the Ubud Art Market and the Kenjen Rice Fields - the pictures aren't doing justice to what we saw, but I guess it gives you a glimpse 😍Loitered around a bit more through the Ubud Palace and street markets and landed at the Puri Museum - which showcases balinese art since the 1800s - I loved it, went through every painting and description while Sidd loitered outside - he's too cultured he says, looking at anymore culture will be too much for us less-cultured people to handle 😂. All paintings were familiar as well - our cultures are so intertwined, even the folklore is the same - the paintings were all stories from panchatantra and amarchitrakatha. 
By the time the sun set, we ended up at Sun Sun Warung, realised it was a famous place - had to wait for a table for 20 min. Food was amazing, we had the Nasi Campur and some yummy green coconut dessert. Walked back in a food coma.  
Sidd's scooty might make a comeback tomorrow as my transport around town - May god save the girls of Ubud :)
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Everyday need not be exploding with novelty, doing nothing with someone you like can be equally comforting. Routine is an underrated luxury. 
Coffees: 2 + 1 :)

steps.title: Sidemen
steps.story:
What a grape day! Morning started with some torrential rains which kept us in the hostel till about 11 am - made for some good conversation with people in the hostel - met David from the US who'd travelled to India twice and after speaking to him we felt like he knew more about India than we did 😒
The rains eased a bit and we dashed out trying to make the most of all the dry time we could. We decided to go to a waterfall - Tukad Cepung, which was an hour away. We thought  if it rains, it rains we'll just travel wet 🤷. Thankfully, it did not rain and the drive to the waterfall through villages and paddy fields was a beautiful one! After some "turn right!!"s (when you actually had to go left) by me and some "oh my god! you should visit a doctor"s by Sidd we reached the waterfall 1.5 hours later. The approach to the waterfall is amazing - it's a short trek after which you enter a cave, wade through a river and then reach the falls - some people said this place is okayish because it's crowded - but I'd still definitely recommend it despite the crowd.
We came back and decided to go for a massage. The music at the massage place was great - some instrumental music ft. light snoring by Sidd, which made for great entertainment for me and the masseuse 😂
The traffic in Ubud was crazy today on account of the Melasti ceremony at Pura Dalem Kangin temple in Tegalalang, Bali. Melasti is a purification ritual performed by Balinese Hindus before Nyepi (the Balinese Day of Silence) - we witnessed the procession on the road while we were driving around - it was quite nice to see so many people dressed alike - dancing, walking, playing instruments! 
We ended up parking our scooty and walking around in the walking streets here. I know I have said it before but this place has a great great vibe - aesthetic cafes everywhere in the smallest of corners, all kinds of shops - you could just sit and watch people here all day and not get bored. 
Got tired and went to a small warung overlooking the rice fields near our hostel - Warung Gauri. Great place, slow service but worth it. We might end up eating all our meals here :) 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Exposure to different people and cultures is quite important to give you a macro perspective in life. Homogeneity sometimes restricts you from  opening up your mind. 
Coffees: 0 :)

steps.title: Ubud Day 3
steps.story:
Today has been the day we've been waiting for - Vishakha Mittal is in Bali to visit us!! 
We woke up to the rain again - but we had lots to do - we had to move, we were excited to meet our friend Vishakha and also looking forward to a day of chasing waterfalls! 
We moved and checked into a great homestay im Ubud called Utu Homestay - what a great find! The rooms are inside a very nice couple's home and are so good at really cheap rates. Each rooms comes with a small kitchenette and a verandah. Please stay here if you ever come to Ubud - highly recommend! 
After checking in and after some hours of Sidd obsessively tracking Vishakha's movements (not complaining - we love sidd and his papa-ness), vishakha finally joined us and we went to Layana Warung - a restaurant we had heard about with a great waterfall view. It did not disappoint. The Warung was atop a hill with a great view - we had some great conversations while we watched the waterfall and food was, as always, yum! We then went to the Kanto Lampo watefall - the reviews labeled it as the instagrammer's hotspot - and that's what it was. It was quite crowded with long lines and they weren't even letting us swim in the water. Quite disappointed, we decided to go to Taman Sari waterfall but ended up asking our grab driver which waterfall is lesser known and better for swimming - he recommended Tibumana waterfall. Thank you so much Mr. grab driver because it was a great recommendation - the waterfall of course had a picturesque walk down, with wooden bridges and jungles, but the best part was that there was no one but us and you could go into the water and take a swim! Sidd was like a child with candy - he was taking dips like this was his Mahakumbh visit 😂. Asked him if he washed all his sins off - he thinks some more dips are needed :) 
We all had a nice swim. While the waterfall was great, the roads in Bali leave us in a constant state of wonder. Every place we go to is so green and beautiful - you just want to stop everywhere and stare. 
We rode back from Tibumana back to our nice homestay, had some downtime and were out and about again in the streets of Ubud - showing everything to Vishakha like we were locals. 😆 
Came across an Indian Restaurant which had a sign outside from Jenny and Martin which read "We came to Bali in 2021 on a "sabbatical" and decided to stay and open our own cafe" - Time for some inspiration for Siddy and Shreya? Maybe some musings required here :p 
Had some smoothie bowls at Kayunan Warung in a traditional Balinese seating - headed back home and ended the night in happy spirits. :) 
Musings from Sidd, Shreya and Vishakha's conversations: Darr k aage jeet hai! Keep taking risks and don't take life so seriously. 
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Ubud Day 4
steps.story:
Today was a day of a lot of screams - most happy, some scared. We had decided to go for river water rafting and ATV and started early - 9 sharp. Mr. Budi, whom we had asked to  organise the day for us, came to pick us up in a v sexy looking, highly modified Innova - which looked like an ATV itself. Mr. Budi was sweet enough to play a remix playlist of Bollywood music with Balinese beats for our benefit. We reached a spot where we were then made to sit in a smaller open van and dropped at another place from where we trekked to the raft. Our guide I think was the best part about this entire activity - Over the years he had learnt some Hindi words and after profiling us (correctly) as Indians he kept telling us to "chalo", then to "chalao our chappu". He was very well versed with bollywood as well - he christened himself as Johnny Lever, Vishakha - Rani Mukherjee and Sidd - Shahrukh Khan. Kept calling all the women "Ati Sundar" - he was a vibe and had us in splits throughout the ride! Vishakha wasn't behind in trying to match his vibe - she kept telling everyone that the three of us were on our honeymoon together just to see the puzzled expressions on everyone's faces 😂
The ride was a 2 hour one with a nice swim in the river towards the end. By the end of the trip Johnny Lever had declared that I will be his wife and Sidd said "toh mai kya karu? Job chhod du?". 
We had lunch, which was part of Mr. Budi's package, and left for our next activity - ATV. I think I really wasn't prepared for what ATV was going to be like. I thought it was going to be as easy as driving a scooty but I was about to be proven wrong :) 
We got on and started - it took me and Vishakha some time to get used to it, Sidd of course was showing off, riding it only with one hand and all. There were some almost falls for me in the beginning - but after that I think I got the hang of it. Sidd disagrees - I could see the terror on his face watching me drive the ATV, turning back every 2 secs saying - "I saw that, you were about to fall - please come tandem" 😂
After 1.5 hours of some serious concentrated driving by me and Vishakha and some fun driving by Sidd, we got done and were dead tired by then. Luckily, our nice homestay couple offered us free spa sessions which was just what we needed. 
While we wanted to paint the town the red at night as well and we ventured out with that agenda - by 9pm the yawns started overpowering our conversations and we were asleep by 10. 😂
Musings from Sidd, Shreya and Vishakha's Conversations: Kitna bhi try karlo bunny, kuch na kuch toh chhutega hi, isliye jahan hai - wahan ka maza utha lena chaiye. 
Sorry, this is Ye Jawani Hai Diwani - but we agree with this quite a bit :) 
Coffees: 0 :)

steps.title: Ubud day 5/6
steps.story:
Day 5 in Ubud was a rainy musical day and day 6 was a lazy day for Vishakha and me - not so much for Sidd :p 
Started day 5 with some V day wishes and then decided to do the Cempuhan Ridge walk - we were told that it's overrated but we still decided to go for it. Went there and realised we should have listened to whoever said it is overrated - it was too sunny, and the walk had no ridge whatsoever - got bored and decided to go to a cafe nearby we'd heard about. On our way we got caught in insane rain - Sidd with his long legs ran away while Vishakha and I got stuck under a random shed, watched the rain and cracked stupid jokes. Finally ended up at Yellow Flower after walking through what felt like an obstacle course - felt like we did a ridge walk there. 
Yellow flower was a quaint vegan restaurant - everything was v healthy and so while we liked the ambience, the food was not suiting our spice hungry pallettes :p 
We came back and tried to go to the Kanjeng rice fields again, but got stuck in the rain again. Sidd had left us to have some adventures of his own - Vishakha and I think he went to meet some of the girls that had gone crazy :) 
When we got back, Sidd surprised us with some V day presents a.k.a junk food and cakes! ❤️
After some rest time, we decided to visit Why Not Bar - known to be the "liveliest bar in Bali" and this wasn't an overstatement. Man, what a great vibe. The band was a local band singing some classic rock songs, the crowd was going crazy and even joining in. One person from the crowd volunteered to sing and we thought it's going to be another bathroom singer performance - but it seems that guy must've had his own band or something cause he sang like a rockstar. Definitely a must visit place in Ubud! 
We walked back home, satisfying some gelato cravings and reached our homestay, decided we didn't have water so walked back to get some and on our way randomly stumbled upon a random local concert happening on the side of the road. Another lovely experience - small crowd just having fun to local songs - while we didn't know the lyrics, we didn't feel like we were missing out. The band was great, the guitarist was even greater. Music surpasses language barriers I guess :) 
The next day the sun was out and I don't know why we decided to go cycling 😆
After some struggle in renting a bike, and some further struggles riding in the traffic, Vishakha and I gracefully bowed out of this activity to watch a movie while Sidd continued on his journey. Finally went to Kanjeng Rice Fields again where Vishakha plucked some rice out of the rice fields like a rice farmer - her true calling I think. 😛
Chilled at Warung Sweet Orange again and ended the night with in room conversions about ghosts and travel. V intellectual :) 
Musings from Vissu, Sidd and Shreya's conversations: It's refreshing to see everyone so happy all around Bali. Everyone's nice to each other, dancing, singing - just having a great time. What are we doing wrong? 
Coffees: 4-5. :)

steps.title: Canggu
steps.story:
3 days in Canguu have been just about good food and a lot of dancing! 
We came to Canguu (a 1 hour cab ride from Ubud) to Roommates Hostel - a beautiful hostel, lovely pool and staff. The dorms are clean and the cafe is a great place to just laze around and read your book. We landed in the pool - made some effort to teach Vishakha some swimming - would like to report that she's managed to learn how to float (somewhat) and keep her head underwater for 30 secs - a great feat I would say :p 
Played some pool volleyball - had an intense neck to neck match where we beat Sidd 😎
In the evening, we went to Motel Mexicola - amazing vibe! Around 9pm everyone gets up on the tables and starts dancing on 90s and 80s tunes. Sidd stood like a bouncer with his fanny pack while Vishakha and I danced - he attempted to dance as well, we think he did quite well - some hip movements were involved :) 
The next day, we found this great great breakfast place - Crate Cafe. Everything there was extra large and extra yummy. The whole cafe had hundreds of photos of patrons everywhere - on the tables, on the walls - made for a fun read while you waited for food. It has a v fancy menu, the portions are daunting which only Sidd could finish. We liked it so much we went there again the next day! 
Took a trip to Finns Beach Club (since we'd heard so much about it) - the view was amazing with the infinity pool and the sea right after - would definitely recommend it if you're a party person. Vishakha and I went into the pool and looked out into the ocean very aesthetically, danced a bit and generally enjoyed the vibe. Sidd didn't like it so much, wasn't his vibe he said. We think he was missing hiranandani babes and boys. ❤️
It has been 15 days since we've been out of India and the day had finally come when we just couldn't pretend we weren't missing Indian food. Ended up ordering some butter chicken and matar paneer and the sounds everyone made after the first bite were the stuff of symphonies. 😂
On the last day - we went to Seminyak to Starbucks Reserve. Vishakha, a coffee lover, was quite excited but ended up finding it overrated - I guess it was. Nothing much to see there apart from marvelling at the size of it.
We walked the streets of Seminyak, lost in conversations - went to a restaurant called the Sea Circus - the place's founder had passed away recently and they'd paid a very nice tribute to him inside the restaurant with his pictures and messages. It was quite nice - especially the crochet frame of a message he probably sent to someone. 
All in all a chill 3 days - would recommend Canguu only if you're interested in good parties and lots of food. 
Musings from Sidd, Vishakha and Shreya's Conversations - Quite tired, the quality of our conversations have deteriorated. We descended to discussing - considering we could all change our surnames to whatever we want, what would we pick? Vishakha picked - Vishakha Kuch Bhi 
Sidd picked - Sidd maps 
What is your pick? 
Coffees : 0 :(

steps.title: Banyuwangi (Mount Ijen)
steps.story:
We have said bye bye to the sunny beaches of Bali and also Vishakha, who has travelled back to India (:/)  - taken a bus and ferry to cross over to Java Island. To anyone travelling via bus from Bali to Java - do not travel by Gunung Harta, take the Mtrans bus! Apart from the disappointment with our bus choices, the travel went smoothly and we reached Banyuwangi, a town in Java by 6pm. Time zones change from Bali to Java - so we were able to gain some time there. Our plan was to do the Kawah Ijen trek the night we reach Banyuwangi for which we had to quickly go and get our health certificate from a clinic - which is required to do the trek. Kawah Ijen is an active volcano with sulphur deposits, so much so that a lot of mining is conducted there. The sulphur makes the lake inside the crater a beautiful blue. It is the largest acidic lake in the world. This is what we were hoping to see. 
We were staying at the Snooze hostel - definitely recommend you stay here wherever they are in Java! The property is lovely - it's a house converted to a hostel with spacious common areas, a garden, lots of plants. The staff is extra sweet too.  Culture in Java was vastly different from what we saw in Bali - A lot quieter and modest (for lack of a better word 😂). There are even signs at a lot of places saying - "This isn't Bali, please reserve your bikinis for the pool and not the streets" :p 
We checked in, quickly ate and tried to catch a nap before we had to start for the trek at 12 a.m. The trek had to be a night trek in order to catch the sunrise at the top.
We had booked a tour from the hostel itself - so some people from the hostel were traveling with us - always nice to talk to fellow travellers from across the world living the same nomadic lifestyle as us. It is funny how this has become the new normal for us.
We got picked up from the hostel and had to travel an hour by car to the point from where we start our trek - it was raining and the drive up in the dark felt quite ominous :p 
We reached the spot and were given a head torch and a gas mask (to protect from sulphur fumes) -met with our guide and our group who had to trek together. Guides here are great as always - our guide's name was Sule and to ensure we stay together he named our group as the Pokemon group. Now every time he shouted 'pika pika' or 'pokemon' we all had to shout our attendance. 😂
The trek was 3.5kms but man it felt like 30kms. The way up was really - and I mean really steep! It was a good thing that it was dark and I couldn't see the way ahead otherwise the sight of the incline would have prompted an about turn from me. We wondered why people didn't just do the trek in the day and I'm sure this is the reason - if you see the entire path you wouldn't want to go :p 
We climbed for 3.5 kms till the rim of the crater, where Sidd attempted to lift mined sulphur weighing around 60kgs like a body builder. All the girls went crazy :p 
From the rim we had to descend into the crater to see the blue fire - which is basically the gas from inside the volcano reacting with the sulphur and burning a bright blue colour. 
The descent was the scariest part of the trek. 
It was completely rocky, there was no defined path, it was dark and raining and the masks made it slightly difficult to breathe. Quite thrilling, I must say. Felt like a roadie 😎
We trekked down and reached the blue fire - it was quite pretty and we were glad that we could see it, there was a possibility that because of the rain we might not be able to. 
Trekked back up - much easier than going down. After some complaints about my "snail's pace" during the trek, Sidd thinks I did quite well :p 
Reached the rim of the crater as the sun came up and as soon light crept in we could see the lake - what a beautiful sight! 🤩  Hands down one of the prettiest places I've seen - the blue right in the middle of the crater was a sight. To sit right at the rim and see this view was an added thrill. The sunrise wasn't as visible since it was cloudy so I wouldn't say we caught the sunrise - but nevertheless we loved it. 
Went back down after some failed photoshoots - slept off on the car ride back and guess what - left my phone in the cab. 😂 I blame it on the sleeplessness - Sidd has other views - he was looking up at the heavens again :p 
Thankfully, people are very sweet here and they gave it back. 
We slept the entire day and are now on our way to Malang via these amazing trains in Indonesia. Cannot help but marvel at how great the entire infrastructure is - the stations are clean, digital to a large extent, the seats and facilities are like travelling business class. Will update on shenanigans in Malang later :) 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Cultures are so dynamic. The difference of a few miles may land you in completely different worlds. The fun is in trying to experience this diversity as much as possible. ❤️
Coffees: 3 :)

steps.title: Malang (Mount Bromo)
steps.story:
Volcano diaries continued as we explored Malang and Mt. Bromo. The past 2 days went in a zombie state considering we've been doing night treks only, but it was all worth it! 
We reached Malang around 2 am and went to our home stay - Inni Home Stay. A very cute place with so many personal touches to make the guests feel at home - they even put up a personalised sign board in front of our room to welcome us. The homestay again has rows and rows of photos of all their guests - we've gone up on the hall of fame too :) 
We woke up after resting a bit and decided to explore Malang. The city is very well planned - wide roads with rows of huge mansions everywhere - took us back to our favourite hobby of just walking around in Indiranagar and looking at beautiful houses. We roamed around in the city and went to the rainbow village that's famous here - it's a small slum area which, as part of a university project of some students here, has been painted with colourful colours and has become a tourist attraction. We ended up spending some time there since we got stuck in the rain - it was quite pretty, but maybe as Indians slums didn't seem quite as attractive to us as compared to our fellow European travellers. 
We visited some cafes and came back home - ready to sleep early since we had to wake up again at 12 am to start the trip to Mt. Bromo. 
Mt. Bromo is another active volcano in Java where you can go upto the crater and peer inside. The road up to the volcano can only be undertaken in these amazing land cruiser jeeps - one of which came to pick us up at our homestay. We were joined by some local tourists in our jeep and the ride up made for some really fun conversations with them. Everyone here seemed to be really obsessed with bollywood - typically all our conversations go -  "So where are you from?" "India" "Ahhh, Shahrukh Khan. That Aishwarya Rai is sexy yeahh?" 😂
Sidd and one of the local tourists here ended up exchanging some appreciation for Alia Bhat and Kiara Advani. :p 
Before we could go to the the crater - the tour involved a trip to a sunrise point - from where you could see the sunrise and the volcano together. The ride up was a bumpy one through the ash fields! Lines of colourful land cruisers riding in a long convoy through the ash fields was such a fun experience - maybe the best part of the trek! 
We reached the sunrise point at around 3 am and it was freezing outside (7-10 degrees) - we ended up renting jackets and therefore, looking like eskimos in all photos. We had to wait for the sunrise till 5 am - which we think could have been planned better. The wait made us quite sleepy (Sidd actually slept off - head down style). 
We ventured out around 5 am to watch the sunrise - I thought it was just beautiful ❤️. The sky was pink, literally, and the volcano smoke right next to the sun rising was the cherry on the cake. Sidd didn't enjoy it as much - he was missing his head-down spot 😂
After the sun had risen, we went to the crater by jeep, to a point after which we had to hike up to the crater. The hike was quite short and easy and the crater was quite scary looking - but what we really liked were the views around the crater. It was just a vast expanse of ash fields, surrounded by green hills - made for some beautiful pictures. You could just sit on the jeep and watch the scenery for hours. 
Going back, the ride was even more fun since we could see the hills around which we couldn't in the night - stopped next to a hill called the "Teletubbies Hill" - since it looked like the hills in the Teletubby cartoons and took fun pictures. The group in our jeep going back was really fun - we were joined by someone from the Netherlands and the entire way back we exchanged all the different things about our cultures - made for a lot of ooohs and aahs. Everyone we meet seems to be a huge fan of pakodas - they call it cauliflower fritters. :p 
We came back and slept like a log - onto Yogyakarta tomorrow. No more treks for some time - I hope! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Everyone may not enjoy the same aspects of an experience. I loved the sunrise, while Sidd loved hiking up to Bromo. The fun part is to share all of this together and indulge in constant banter along the way. 
Coffees: 5 :)

steps.title: Yogyakarta
steps.story:
Yogyakarta/Jogjakarta / Djodjakarta - this place has multiple names and holds a lot of significance for Indonesia - historically. We reached Jodja (how people refer to the city here) via a lovely train - this time a day train so we could see the lovely views on the way. We were staying at Hubs Hostel - a nice hostel, though the rooms are a little poorly ventilated. 
After some much needed rest, we went out to Malioboro Street - which is the main  mall road kind of street here. The street is equivalent to Mumbai's causeway - rows and rows of shops selling local sweets, batik printed clothes and other eatables. We roamed around, I tried some local chocolates - didn't like them very much :p 
We also tried Bakpia, a local delicacy here - we must've crossed some 100 shops selling Bakpia and I had hopes from it - but it wasn't very good. :( 
At the end of Malioboro Street is a beautiful town square - all buildings in Jodja have Dutch architecture, which is quite beautiful if you set aside the colonial atrocities.  
We had dinner and slept off - quite tired and also because we had to start the next day early. 
Woke up and started the day with visiting a water castle here (Taman Sari) - the photos seemed great but we would not recommend going there. There's nothing to see, the building is not maintained very well, please skip it if you come here. Next on the list was Sungai Mudal, a waterfall -  1 hour drive from the main city. We had hired a bike to go there.
Some background on how we decide on which places to visit in a city - I suggest we go to a place, Sidd says no (his initial response to most things :p), I insist, Sidd does extensive research for 5 days, I still insist, on the day of travel he says "are you still sure?" Goes on to mention some things that may not be right, I still insist - then we reach and Sidd invariably ends up loving it shouting "Maine toh bola hi tha chalte hai". 
So that's how we reached Sungai Mudal and man, what a place! The ride to it was through rice fields, up the hills and past quaint villages. The views were, in Sidd's words, sasta Switzerland :) 
The whole area has been made into a sort of picnic spot - there are catchments made out of the waterfall into these crazy blue water pools nestled inside a hill so there are tall trees and a jungle all around. You can swim in the pools, which are all freshwater, there's even some fish in them! The whole experience was unreal - definitely recommended. Skip the Borobodur sunrise and go here - that's what we did. No surprise that Sidd loved it ofcourse 😁
We started to ride back and it started pouring heavily so we had to stop and take shelter. We thought it'd be for 15-20 min, ended up being one hour and the rain still hadn't stopped so we decided to just ride back in the rain. Got soaked and kept making ourselves feel better by calling this an adventure 😂. It was quite fun actually. 
In the evening, I went to the Vrendenburg museum - which showcases the freedom struggle of Indonesia against colonial rule, very much like ours. Sidd politely declined to accompany me - said we shouldn't dwell on the past :p 
The museum was amazing. It's inside, what used to be a Dutch guest house and is very well done - learnt a lot. 
We leave for a small town called Bandung tomorrow. 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Any event could easily be looked at as positive or tedious - depends on perspective. Seems all is in your control really! 
Coffees: 3 :)

steps.title: Bandung
steps.story:
After a very long yet very scenic train ride we reached Bandung and checked into our hotel. As usual, it was raining -.-  but we still decided to go out. My first thought walking around Bandung was that this is an army area - and sure enough we found out we're in a cantonment. Naturally, I felt quite at home and nostalgic :)
When we inquired at our previous hostel what we should do in Bandung, everyone raved about this "party street" called Braga. It's the place to go at night they said. We got quite excited and so ventured out in the rain to Braga only to find it quite underwhelming. I mean it's a nice street, a lot of cafes and bars but it wasn't very lively and probably the rain put a dampener too. We ate some yum food at Gas Inc. and came back home. 
The next day, we decided to take it easy - hired a Scooty and went riding around town. Bandung is like a hill station - some parts of the town therefore have winding streets, pine trees and if you go high enough, the clouds descend on you. 
We went to a really nice cafe called Armor Kopi which was up a hill and had a lovely garden - had some himachal style lemon tea and enjoyed the sun. In the evening we went to a place called Sultan Agung restaurant - food was average but the menu was the size of a novel. Took us 20 min to get through it. Would definitely recommend it if you want to catch up on some reading :p 
The next day was the big day! Big as in, we had something planned for this day 😄 
We were going to Kawah Putih (means White Crater in Indonesian) in the town of Ciwidey - another hill station 2 hours away from Bandung, famous for its tea plantations. We had hired a car with our very nice driver Mr. Rudi. We explored options of going via a tour or on scooty - but after factoring in rain and our adventures in Yogya, we decided to take a car. It was a great decision, Rudi was extremely nice, telling us tidbits about Bandung and Indonesian culture - played really nice music all the way too. 
We reached Kawah Putih - which is basically a blue crater lake similar to Ijen but here you can go right up to the lake. The view was amazing 😍 Sidd and I tried some cringe photography with our tripod - one result is uploaded - DM for more embarrassing pictures :p 
This place is also famous for its strawberries - and so we ended up buying 1 kg of strawberries 😂. Not sure how we'll finish it all - but alas, we're a generation of impulses. 
From there, we started for Kawah Rengannis - famous for hot springs! - But the ride to Kawah Rengannis was the ultimate beauty. I've seen tea gardens before but this was even more beautiful because of the clouds right on top of them and the slight rain making the green pop. 🍃
To reach the hot springs in Rengannis, you have to walk through a suspension bridge - which is beautiful, but I was too scared to look down. Sidd was walking on it like it was a park and became quite popular with the aunties on the bridge who wanted their photos clicked. Girls going crazy everywhere :p 
Reached the hot springs and met some nice guides there who scammed us for some money but showed us all the things we should do to truly enjoy the experience. 
So we first had to do some "mudding" which is basically rubbing volcanic ash on your body - it's supposed to be really good for your skin and can make you look youthful. Sidd agrees, he swears he's looking 10 years younger - has decided to start carrying his ID card everywhere - in case he gets carded at a club, he says. 😂
Once the mud dries, you can go and relax in these amazing hot springs which are like a warm hug, while you watch the hills covered in pine trees and the clouds roaming about around you. Once you're done relaxing and washing off the mud, you're supposed to take a cold shower in the waterfall running right there! Leaves your legs numb but also leaves you feeling really fresh. A great, great experience - definitely one of our favorite things we did in Indonesia. 
The way back to the parking was through a cable car - not a lot of car though - they basically make you sit on a garden swing hanging from the cable and send you to the other side. I think it was fun - it should be noted though, that I refused to look down the entire time. :) 
We're back in Bandung. Off to Jakarta tomorrow. More later! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversation: We're not musing anything. Just binging on House during all the free time. :p 
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Jakarta
steps.story:
We have reached Jakarta - not a big fan of the cities now that we've spent most of our time in quaint, green towns. Jakarta honestly reminds us of BKC, Mumbai :p 
Still, we've tried to do some things here. out hotel La Boheme is amazing. Very boho, lovely rooms and a very nice rooftop cafe to chill at. 
The first day we went to Bloc M, which was described as a trendy place to hang out but ended being a mall 😞 
Roamed around and came back. 
The next day, we decided to go our separate ways - me to an antique market and then a museum and Sidd in the hostel with his laptop :p 
The antique market in Menteng was quite cool, found some really old and cool stuff there to look at. From there I went to Monas - a national monument in Jakarta which had a nice museum. While I was there, I guess Sidd just couldn't bear any time apart since he literally "ran" to Monas.  
Ended up going back home to hide from the heat and ventured out in the evening to Kota Tua - old town Jakarta with really pretty dutch buildings. From there we went to Glodok - Chinatown in Jakarta - which seemed really shady and we had to leave quickly since Sidd was convinced someone will kidnap us. 
Came back home and ended the night with some bye bye Indonesia cheers! 
Onto Singapore tomorrow. ❤️
Coffees: 1

steps.title: Singapore Day 1&2
steps.story:
What a city, Singapore! We've fallen in love with it. 
We landed at Changi airport in the afternoon. Even though after backpacking across small towns in Indonesia, any development would seem like a lot - Singapore was another level. We seamlessly took the metro from the airport to our hotel which is on Bencoolen Street - a very nice area - would definitely recommend staying here. Everything here is as smooth as a knife through butter - all information is user friendly, easy to understand and readily available. The entire city and each aspect within it is planned really meticulously. 
Since we have only 3 days here - we didn't waste much time after checking in and quickly changed to go to Gardens by the Bay at Marina Bay Sands. It's quite nice - but more than the gardens I enjoyed walking along the water front. Roamed around the MBS mall and wandered through all the Gucci's and Cartier's of the world in our skechers. 😂
From there we had to go to Grange Rd to visit a relative. Taking a cab feels like a crime here with the amazing public transport, you don't even mind walking a bit since the weather is great. Had a great time with family and some amazing Indian food. Also met the cutest little puppy - Rocket! 🥹
Roamed around Orchard Rd, came back home and read up all there is to read about the history of Singapore. These days I've assumed the role of tour guide to Sidd - I need to read up on all historical facts about a place and point them out (tldr only) at appropriate moments.  
Next day was Sentosa Day!! We woke up early to get there asap so we could skip the long lines. Universal studios is beautiful and a lot of fun! Both of us went completely crazy - like school kids, running around from ride to ride. I cajoled Sidd into coming with me on a rollercoaster named Battlestar Gallactica - as soon as we were done I heard him shout - "I'm too old for rollercoasters!!" 😂 
Would recommend to definitely visit on a weekday and take the express pass if you're willing to pay double - the lines become crazy long and make you really tired. You can skip the Jurassic park and Disney rides in my opinion if you're pressed for time. 
After we were done with Universal Studios, we went to the Harry Potter interactive experience - being a huge Harry Potter fan, I was the most excited for this and it did not disappoint 😍. Everything was exactly how you saw it in the movies or imagined when you were reading the books. You had your own wand which you could use to perform magic, the whole place is really well done - I could go again and again! Sidd and I had a wand battle in the end - 10 points to whoever guesses the winner :) 
After Harry Potter, we wandered into the Casino - we stood at the Roulette table with our 25$ worth chips like a boss while people next to us were betting some big money. Lost half of that, quietly thanked roulette aunty and went to cash in the remaining chips 😂 
In the evening, we just went around exploring the city - ate at the famous Maxwell hawker centre, walked across Chinatown (a complete opposite to the Chinatown in Jakarta :p) to Clarke Quay, walked around the iconic Fullerton Hotel, discussed that staying at Fullerton is part of my bucket list, while Sidd confessed that his bucket list currently only includes the wish that I walk faster. 🙄
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Anybody giving job in Singapore, please DM. We're very interested. :p
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Singapore Day 3
steps.story:
Since we're mentally children - we landed up in Sentosa again the next day to check out the Adventure Cove Water Park. It was a lot of fun - especially since it was a week day and there was no crowd and hence no lines. Please witness 30yr old Sidd splashing about in the wave pool 😂
3-4 rides were shut for maintenance - would've been more fun if all the rides were available, but no worries since Sidd and I went on the rides that were open at least 4 times :p 
We got done pretty early and decided to explore Siloso Beach on Sentosa Island. Luckily, we were able to get cycles and ride around the beach and through Sentosa. What a lovely island - a compact place where you can find everything. Definitely a bucket list item to come back and spend some time here. 
On the way back we ate at the Food Republic hawker centre at Vivocity. While Maxwell is iconic - I enjoyed Food Republic much more! It was livelier and had better options. If you're visiting you should definitely try either Food Republic at Vivocity or the hawker centre at MBS. 
Came back home and went to meet some friends we have in the city. Made for a fun evening with lovely food. We visited the building where Sidd stayed when he was living in Singapore. After a nostalgic walk, we went back home - to get ready for tomorrow - onto KL, Malaysia! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Someone I know very rightly once said, it's not okay to be childish but it's very important to be childlike. Acting old is overrated 😛
Coffees: 2 :)

steps.title: Kuala Lumpur
steps.story:
We have done 4 things in KL 
1. Sleep 
2. Cook 
3. Watch Kim's Convenience all day 
4. Eat 
That's it. 
Also went to watch Chhava - v bad movie. Sidd left the hall midway and sat outside (he didn't even have internet :o) while I watched the whole movie.
Many thanks to my dad for his netflix password and quick turnaround for all OTP requests. Also many thanks to Sidd's dad for enabling us access to this lovely room in KL, of which, we have taken full advantage. 
Dads FTW! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Travel is not about sightseeing, it's about experiencing different velocities of life. (please contact Sidd to understand the meaning of this profound thought) 
Coffees: 2 :)

steps.title: Cameron Highlands
steps.story:
Hellooo from Cameron Highlands! 
We've come to the hill town of Malaysia, famous for tea and good weather. 
The weather indeed was good - maybe a bit too cold for me, but perfect for Sidd. The AQI was amazing - which according to our tour guide was not so good - Sidd and I looked at each other when he said this, a silent look of shame passing between us thinking of what we put up with back home. 
The place is laid back, a lovely weekend getaway for a lot of local tourists. 
The first day we just roamed around Tanah Rata (the town where we were staying), went to a nearby town - Brinchang (15 min away), where Sidd paid money to cook his own food. 
The next day we'd booked a half day tour from the hostel. The tour took us around the lovely tea plantations here and then also to a cafe run by the plantation which had a lovely view 😍. Some really nice tea as well - they had different flavours of tea, I loved the caramel flavored one. 
We then went to the Mossy Forest, which used to be a great jungle trek but now has become quite touristy. Apart from a great viewpoint and seeing pitcher plants up close, not much to do there - very skippable. 
We met some really nice people on the tour. Almost everyone had been travelling for many months and had plans to go to Australia/new zealand - take up some job there for a bit and then travel again. We were blown away, once more, by this completely different world where people are living these nomadic lives. 
Do we have it in us to do something similar? Some musings required here :p 
There are multiple trekking trails around Cameron Highlands all numbered and defined which you can do on your own. After the tour, Sidd had planned to do trail no. 10 but I guess the treks in his dreams were seeming more challenging to him so he took a nap instead. :p 
We stayed at the Bricks hostel - a very nice, cozy hostel - definitely recommended. It has a very nice common room, which is where we spent our evening the  second day chatting with other travellers who were very very surprised to know that we don't cook our own food in India. Their expressions were of utter shock. They kept referring to the cook as a "private chef" which is a luxury reserved only for royalty in their country (they were from Italy and Australia). 😂
It was really funny for us to acknowledge our privilege while also trying to explain to them that it's not a big deal. At one point I desperately wanted to say "arre you know, kaam wali aunty" but  I knew they wouldn't understand the sentiment. :P 
They were really fascinated with this "Indian concept" and went on to ask questions like "so then, can you ask them to make whatever you want? Or do they make what they want?", "is it like a private restaurant?" 😂 
We were very amused while explaining how house-help aunties work in India and realised we are quite lucky, help wise. 
Tomorrow we go on to Georgetown! 
More from there ❤️
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Biryani chaiye yaaaar. 
Coffees: 0 :)

steps.title: George Town
steps.story:
We set off from Cameron and reached Georgetown 4 hours later via a very unpleasant bus ride. I was almost about to throw up and had a bag ready in my hand. Thankfully didnt have to use it :)

We checked into a wonderful homestay/hotel called Li's Inn and set off to grab something to eat. Georgetown is a UNESCO world heritage site and we were staying right in the centre! There are wonderful tiny lanes with beautiful art and shops, very similar to Galle Fort in Sri Lanka. 

Walked around, found some local street food at Red Garden but decided to eat well at Gravybaby. Every lane here is wonderful to walk by, its a small town so you can get from one end to the other in no time. We ended the day with some drinks and dinner, singing along to a live band on Love Lane. 

The next day we went to see the Clan Jetties of Penang. Quite underwhelming, just a bunch of old houses made on the water. I rented a cycle (finally found a road bike) and went all the way up to Batu Ferringhi. A beautiful ride along the coast, with quite a few changes in elevation adding to the heart pump. 

Day 3 (today) was basically spent in the homestay. We lazed around all day, it was too hot to go out till about 4 PM. Finally, we got out of our slumber and went to grab some food - spicy noodles at Yeap Noodle House. Ended the day with some delivered food in the homestay itself - it was just one of those days where you want to take it easy :)

P.S. - First post written by Sidd (as an experiment)

steps.title: Langkawi Day 1&2
steps.story:
Arrived in the touristy Langkawi after a bus+ferry combo which I was sure we would miss. Thanks to the cab driver for making us catch it. 

Checked into the Seven Stones homestay with the most welcoming owner, Mas. She was very sweet and kept asking us how we are doing. I would recommend everyone to stay in or around Pantai Cenang - this is the area where most things are happening in Langkawi. Spent the first day just loitering the streets and ended with dinner at a local warung.

Day 2: Scooter Diaries
Rode all over Langkawi island with a 110CC scooter. The roads here are just amazing even though the sun is very harsh. 
Homestay -> Skycab -> Pantai Kok -> Temurun waterfall -> Gunung Raya -> Kuah Jetty -> Back home

After 7 hours outside, I was exhausted and got back, showered and napped. Gunung Raya is the top most point of Langkawi with amazing views, much better than paying RM 85 for a cable car ride. 

Set out again in the evening to Cenang beach, which was bustling with beachside fire shows and many tourists walking around. Didnt feel like eating so just grabbed some fresh fruit for RM 5 and some duty-free chocolate (yes, Langkawi is a duty-free island. Alcohol is very very cheap). Had a really long day, so got a nice foot massage and called it a day :)

steps.title: Langkawi Day 3&4
steps.story:
After a short break - I am back at updating you'll of our daily shenanigans. Thanks to Sidd for keeping the updates coming in my absence :p 
Day 3 - Sidd came to pick me up at the airport to my surprise and elation :D 
The airport is a small one and on our drive back we stopped to watch the planes land.
Didn't do much on day 3 apart from eating all our meals at this Indian restaurant, walking on the beach and watching the fire show, which was quite good. 
Day 4 - We'd booked the jet ski island tour and had to get up early in the morning to go to the beach where we had to start our tour. I had never driven one before but Sidd claimed to be a pro - maybe that's why we ended up toppling over in the sea in the first 5 mins :) 
After this fun salt bath, Sidd got the hang of driving the jetski and then the speeds at which he went were terrifying 🙈
The ride is not for the fainthearted - the jetski goes over choppy waves and the entire time you keep feeling like you're going to fall or get flung across the sea. I hung on for dear life while Sidd had the time of his life - he kept asking me if I wanted to ride and I politely kept declining, very happy being a passenger princess :p 
We went to multiple islands on the jetski - one of them had a nice cafe which was blasting punjabi music and then moved on to songs from the dirty picture - fun to see all firangs grooving to oo lala tu hai meri fantasy 😂
This particular island had something known as the miracle border - which is basically a natural border between the sea and a large freshwater lake. We swam in the lake and then hopped on back on our jetskis to go back in the sea. 
All in all a thrilling experience - definitely recommend. Tip: Go slow! 
In the evening we went to a nice cocktail bar and ordered a drink called "I don't know" - which is basically the bartender's choice for you. The drink was so good but when we asked to order it again - the bartender refused saying she couldn't make it again since "she didn't know" :p 
Some begging later, she said she'll try and she did deliver something similar. 
Ate at the Indian restaurant again! Came back home to get ready to go to Krabi, Thailand. More tomorrow. 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Distance makes the heart grow fonder, but familiarity has yet not bred contempt. ❤️
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Ao Nang (Krabi) - V1
steps.story:
After a long travel day (10 hrs) which included a ferry ride, a long bus ride and a relatively short tuk tuk ride we reached Ao Nang, Krabi - a stark difference from the quiet streets of Langkawi, Ao Nang is so lively and vibing, the spirit is infectious and instantly puts you in a good mood. The first few days we stayed at K Bunk hostel - a very nice find by Sidd. The hostel has amazing staff who are travellers themselves and are volunteering at the hostel. They host activities every day to get people talking to each other which are super fun! The day we reached, it was musical bingo night at the hostel and it was sooo much fun! Everyone was playing and singing along to the songs - I was forced to sing some of the songs on the mic as well. The volunteers do a great job at organizing the entire thing, pumping everyone up - it was a very wholesome experience. After the game, they were to take everyone out for a pub crawl - which Sidd and I, the old people that we are, opted out of and went to bed at 11 pm :P 
The next day, while walking around, we spontaneously decided to go kayaking in a mangrove forest nearby. Quickly booked a tour and reached the kayak centre 30 min away - got our short training and hopped on to our kayaks with a group of 6 kayaks including our guide. After some initial accusations by Sidd that I'm "doing some random shit" and not kayaking properly, I am proud to report that eventually he was very happy with my progress and even complimented my improvement. 😂
The tour was amazing - definitely a must do activity in Krabi! The mangroves felt right out of a movie, the water was reducing by the minute and so the entire ride became quite adventurous since we got stuck at multiple places and had to maneuver our way out. It made for a good workout as well - I can definitely see some muscals. 😄
Came back, watched the fire show they had organised at the hostel and retired early. 
Next day, we had my chacha coming down to meet us! We moved hotels and met up with him - Got 2 massages in the same day and in the evening headed out to the Ao Nang night market. The night market is lovely, there's a lot of shopping that you can do, but the best part is the umpteen number of food stalls serving all kinds of food. We tried different things and took some fun pictures with food we didn't have the stomach to try :p 
Exiting the night market, we heard some good rock music playing in a restaurant but when we tried to get a table, guess what they told us - "No indians allowed" 😂
I was quite annoyed, while chacha found it funny and tried to convince them that he was born in Kenya and hence they should give us a table :p 
We didn't get the table and left from there. Not that you'd be allowed entry but please do not visit the Rock Bar in Ao Nang - they are bad peepuls. :( 
After some more shopping, we ended up at the Reggae Bar, which had nice live music playing. We had a fun night of great conversations, made a train and sang along with the singer and eventually ended up eating at an Indian restaurant 😂
Nothing better than home food - like desis we ordered jeera rice, yellow dal and jeera aloo and had a lot of fun chatting with the staff in Hindi. Called it a night after that! 
Day 4 - Chacha was to go back in the afternoon, so we just went to the Ao Nang beach and a nice restaurant by the beach called Reeve. Our choices in restaurants had become quite high end since we had an adult now accompanying us refusing to let us pay the bills 😂 - Love being treated like kids ❤️ 
We have 2 more nights left in Krabi - more later on what we get up to. 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's and Chacha's conversations - Other people's actions sometimes anger you - wisdom is in finding the humour in these situations and shaking it off 😎
Coffees: Tooo many 🙈

steps.title: Ao Nang (Krabi) - V2
steps.story:
Last 3 days in Krabi - we checked into Avani Resort, thanks to Sidd's parents Club Mahindra Membership 😅 - and were given a room in a part of the resort which seemed to be reserved for Indians I feel. The resort is great, a lovely infinity pool and a nice room. So we decided to just take advantage of the resort and relax. 
Apart from swimming in the pool and some gymming (by Sidd), we also went to the Railay - which is a short boat ride away from Ao Nang beach. 
Railay is a quieter version of Ao Nang. It has a lot of places to stay and a place where you can do some rock climbing - it had some amazing trails but they looked quite dangerous and so I was very happy to just look and not do :) 
Railay also has beautiful caves within it which opens into the Phrang Na beach - not a very wide beach but clear waters and a cave you can swim into. The water looked so good and tempting, but I had stupidly not packed any swimwear and so I just watched Sidd splash about in the water while I attempted to click hazy pictures of him. A must visit in Krabi - you can also think of spending a night at Railay, it seems like it becomes quite lively at night. 
The rest of the days were spent in the pool, reading some books and eating yum food - which included satisfying dosa cravings at one of the umpteen Indian restaurants here. 
Tomorrow we go to Koh Tao - we've heard it's heavenly - let's hope it is! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: We think we need to get some help to deal with the addiction of watching House MD all the time.  
Coffees: 4 :)

steps.title: Koh Tao - Day 1&2
steps.story:
Koh Tao is everything everyone said it was going to be and even better. So much so that we've decided to skip Koh Samui altogether and stay all days here only till we leave for Bangkok. 
The ferry from Krabi to Koh Tao was around 3 hours and a little uncomfortable. We reached and checked into Sunrise hotel - which is right on the beach and has an amazing view. We rested for a bit and then set out in the evening. The streets in Koh Tao are lively, lined with multiple restaurants, hostels and diving schools - we ended up eating at Angel's bistro which had some amazing red thai curry and really sweet staff. After that we walked around the beach and waited till 9:30 pm - to go attend the famous Queen's Cabaret Show here - and oh my god it was the most fun show we've seen in a while. The entire show is run by the LGBTQ community in Koh Tao and is a mix of singing, dancing and some other fun performances. It was just tooo much fun - even Sidd enjoyed it quite a bit after some initial discomfort 😂
The next day, we woke up and decided to hit some of the beaches here - first stop was Chalok Baan Kao Bay - all the beaches here are pristine! Clear blue waters, white sand, fish and coral all around if you just look down. We swam a bit there, had some food and then decided to go to Freedom beach - which is where we had our first injury of the trip 😭. I was walking barefoot, trying to fix my snorkel mask and ended up stepping on a sea urchin - got stung and had to quickly go to a clinic. It wasn't a very bad sting, just a couple of spines stuck in my heel - which they removed and put a bandage on. I just had to wait for a day before I could swim again. We couldn't get into the water that day then - so we just chilled, went to Tanote Bay in the evening - watched people cliff jump and generally admired the view and called it a day. 
More tomorrow. 
Coffees: 3 :)

steps.title: Koh Tao - Day 3/4/5
steps.story:
We are spending our days in Koh Tao quite leisurely. We fell into the trap of trying out the highly advertised, highly commercialised full day snorkeling tour. The first stop and the best stop was Koh Nang Yuan - a small island 10 min away which is idyllic, for lack of a better word. There are no plastic bottles allowed on this island - it's a self sustained island with no help from the government band it's beautiful ❤️
We did a lot of snorkeling - saw dead coral and a lot of fishes. After that, the whole day included us jumping off the boat into the sea and snorkeling - there were 5 total stops and honestly, we were pretty done with snorkeling after the second one, except for when I got to see a huuuge 150yr old turtle - what a beautiful creature - the pictures do not do justice. Sidd did not come in the water to see the turtle, he thought the turtle would go crazy :) 
If you're here, you should avoid the tour - just go to Nang Yuan yourself with some snorkeling masks and enjoy. 
We chilled the next couple of days, walking around, trying new restaurants and finding out weird things about this island - Koh Tao is apparently known as the murder island of Thailand - people mysteriously/suspiciously die here! We saw a dead body on the beach one day - I've uploaded a photo. Since then, I feel everything is eerie here. 
Sidd is quite irritated with my conclusions 😂
Today we went to the John Sewan point - I hadn't done much research about the hike up, and Sidd told me it was a 44 min hike. The hike will basically turn you into spiderman since there is no clear path and you have to climb up rocks and ropes - I was ready to give up after 10 min when Sidd chose to tell me that it's only a 15 min hike 🙄 - See, this island is convincing people to torture other people :p 
We reached the top and the view was beautiful, quite dangerous to get there, but beautiful! 
We chilled on the freedom beach again and have now checked into a new hotel - to our delight it has a smart TV - so it's a tough choice between watching Dr. House or watching people dance at a bar - what are we going to choose? Only time will tell. 
More later 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Superstition is evil, patience is important :p 
Coffees: 0

steps.title: Koh Tao - Day 6/7/8
steps.story:
We have lazed around so much that I'm tired of lazing around now. 
Last few days in Koh Tao - we found a really nice cafe called Happy Land and then we ended up going there almost everyday 😂
Sidd and I finally went for a yoga class - quite weird to have a firang teach us yoga saying "please do the downward dog pose nowww" when all she was doing was surya namaskar! :p 
The class was really nice though - some workout after soo long was a good change. 
Weird events continued every time we went out - we mysteriously lost items, Sidd got injured as well - this island is spooky. 
Sidd tried to climb a huge rock to cliff dive - but couldn't because he got injured. I didn't even attempt it - very aware of my strengths and weaknesses. :) 
Discovered some other really nice cafes - definitely go to Lazy Coconut and Factory cafe if you're here. 
We also went to fishbowl - a really popular restaurant here, sat on the beach and did some stargazing using an app which told us what we were seeing (sounds romantic but was a very scientific exercise 😛). 
Chased some sunsets, finished 2 netflix shows 😂 and are now on our way to Bangkok on a ferry with the cutest lidl furry co-passenger :p 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: After a heated debate on whether India is owed reparations from our colonial oppressors, we have agreed to not debate on this topic again 😂
Points to whoever guesses correctly who was for and who was against.
Coffees: 0 :)

steps.title: Bangkok
steps.story:
We were somewhat pleasantly surprised by Bangkok! We had only a day here but we managed to have quite a lot of fun. 
The first day, after a long day of ferry + van + flight + cab, we rested for a bit and then went to visit the food market at IconSiam - a popular mall here but the market does not make you feel like you're in one. We had to take a short boat ride to reach the mall, the boat parks right at the entrance. The food market was so much fun - we tried a Thai appetizer called Sago Pak Mor - which was nice albeit a little gooey. Got fascinated by all the weird stuff being sold - including crickets and scorpions and live shrimp salad - we did not have the stomach to try all that, literally. 
Bought some fruit and ate it by the water - Sidd did not appreciate doing aalti-paalti on the floor and eating like a peasant - he did not want to stoop to my level, he said :p 
We then went to Khao San Road, a lively road we had heard a lot about. After coming here, I officially declare that I have become old because I could not get out of that street soon enough! The street was too noisy with bars blasting music at horrific decibel levels and their solicitors getting in your face to convince you to visit - oh my god it was overwhelming. We quickly left - tried the Tuk Tuk on the way back and slept. 
The next day, we visited Wat Pho - a famous temple here which has the reclining Buddha. It was beautiful! The entire complex is very aesthetic with ornate stupas and bonsai trees. The reclining Buddha is massive and has intricate prints at the feet of the Buddha. It's really nice to walk around the entire temple with Buddhist chants playing in the background all around. Even Sidd, an ardent avoider of temples, acquiesced to having a good time! 
In the evening, we went around exploring the parks in Bangkok - we went to Benchakitti Park and Lumphini Park - both beautiful, while Benchakitti included a comprehensive sports complex and a lake, Lumphini only had a huge running track. Sidd made multiple attempts at making me run, hang from bars, walk fast and do all other sorts of monkey activities and then accused me of torturing him by not being good at any of this. 😂
After doing things that he likes, we went to do things that I like - eat desserts! 😋 
We went to June Pang on Songthat street where you get this amazing caramel toast with ice cream and it is the yummiest thing ever!! Instantly puts you in a good mood - must visit if you're here. I already wish I could visit it again. 
After that, we went to Elvis Suki - one of the cheap Michelin star restaurants in Bangkok and had some really tasty noodles and chicken. 
A very nice end to the day - we're now getting ready to say bye bye to Thailand and go to Cambodia tomorrow. 
More later! 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Physical activity is very important. (This seems like a musing from one person only :p) 
Coffees: 0. Hoping to have a good one soon.

steps.title: Siem Reap
steps.story:
We have come to the land of temples - Cambodia! Got off to a rough start - considering we were singled out during immigration since we were Indians - were taken to a different room and interrogated. Apparently that's what happens with all Indians - a bit annoying honestly - but once we got over that and entered the country, we noticed the people here are extremely sweet here, quite refreshing after Thailand, where people were mostly transactional. 
We checked into our hostel - Lub D - great hostel, amazing vibe, it also has a very nice pool. The first day, we didn't do much, except roam around places close to our hostel - we went to the riverside night market and the famous Pub street, went to this bar called Laundry after we saw a band setting up but the band took forever to start playing and they weren't serving any food so we left - priorities! 
The next day we decided to visit the killing fields museum here which depicts the horrific Khmer Rouge regime that Cambodia went through till the 1980. The museum was very well made though extremely sad - the genocide was explained in gory details, they have even displayed the bones recovered of the victims that were killed. After learning a lot about this sad history, we decided to stay indoors for the day since it's tooo hot to stay outside in the day - ended up watching 21 and 22 Jump Street 😂
Day 3 was about temple runs. The plan was that I will go on tuk tuk and go about my visit in my own way, without Sidd hurrying me along (:p) and Sidd will do a circuit of the temples on a cycle. We had to leave at 12 but looking at the heat it didn't make sense for Sidd to cycle - so I went alone on a tuk tuk we hired to show me 3 temples - Ta Phrom (tree temple), Bayon and ofcourse, Angkor Wat! 
My tuk tuk driver, Mr. Reaksmey was extremely sweet, he explained how I should go about the temples, had got a water cooler with him so I had cold water and also kept giving me cold wet wipes after every temple 🙈
The first temple I visited was Ta Phrom - also known as the tree temple and is famous as the temple where Lara Croft was shot. The temple was apparently completely ruined when ASI offered to help restore it funded by MEA, India in the 1980s to what it is today. Next, I visited the Bayon temple, which was my favourite temple - it's mostly like a ruin, you have to climb across all its sections, but that's what gives it its charm, I guess. Angkor Wat was nice, but maybe a bit overhyped in my opinion - or maybe I was just too drained from the heat to enjoy it.
