I came back and slept, while Sidd left at 5 for a 32 km cycle trip across all the temples - came back at 8. We quickly finished packing and eating to catch our first overnight bus to Koh Rong - another idyllic island. Please witness Sidd, quite excited to experience his first sleeper bus experience 😂
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: I have finally been able to get Sidd interested in the history and culture of a place, so much so that going to the museum was his idea! Small wins :)

steps.title: Koh Rong
steps.story:
What could go wrong in Koh Wrong? Nothing, since all people do here is sit by the beach all day and relax - and that's what we did as well :p 
We reached and ofcourse loved where we were staying - Onederz hostel - right on the beach, with comfortable seating, so you can sit there all day with a book while you enjoy the sea breeze. We sat for a bit and then got ready to go to Nestival - a famous party here, organized by one of the hostels, we'd heard quite a bit about it and decided to check it out. Walked on the beach to get there and were greeted by a sea of people all ready to party :p 
We were given tshirts and some paint to get creative with body art - I did some drawing on Sidd to mark my territory - lest the girls go crazy :p 
People there had written really funny stuff on themselves - from flags of their country to funny captions it was all there. Around 3 the sports events start, where you team up with people there and participate in all sorts of games - we teamed up with Tommy and Ollie, a couple of "lads" from England (:p) and participated in the sack race, we didn't win 😂. The events were to go on well into the evening and the party was supposed to go on till early morning - we had been there for 1.5 hours and unanimously decided that we're too old for this :p We were already missing our beach chair and kindle and so we left, went back and ate lunch. 😂
The evenings around the hostel are even more beautiful with music and lights all around. This is also the time when the Khmer New Year is being celebrated here, so the locals would randomly gather around and dance to local songs and invite everybody to join - very wholesome. 
The next day, we rented a scooty to explore the other beaches - quickly realised exploring here meant quite a bit of treacherous off-roading - please witness Sidd trying to drive the scooty with his legs flailing about, hoping to gain some balance :p 
Went to Coconut beach - a beautiful beach, even more than Long Set beach (where we're staying). Sidd did some jumps from the jetty while I tried the nice swing they'd installed in the water. 
Watched some fly boxing at the hostel - both Sidd and I finished one book each in 2 days! Played chess with some makeshift pawns - Sidd beat me - I argued it was beginners luck :p 
Tomorrow we go to Phnom Penh to start our journey towards Vietnam. 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Live and let live should be your mantra - but some deal breakers are allowed.

steps.title: Phnom Penh
steps.story: Only a transit spot - we came here, went for a long walk in a lot of heat and we left 😂

steps.title: Ho Chi Minh City
steps.story:
We have reached Ho Chi Minh City after a very weird immigration process, where we entered without having to show our faces to an officer - our kind bus officials took our passports and returned a stamped one after we crossed over 😂
We're staying at Meander Saigon hostel - the best hostel we've stayed in till now - extremely clean, a special mention to the bathrooms (those who've received pictures will understand :p). 
The day we reached, we went to Nguyen walking street, tried pizza slices and Banh Mis and retired for the night. 
The next day, we started early to go to the War Remnants Museum - a very well made museum on the Vietnam War or as the Vietnamese call it - "The American War". Realised how too much power in the hands of one leads to abuse so easily. :( 
Quickly grabbed another Banh Mi and some salted coffee at Grandma Lu's before we were picked up for our tour to the Cu Chi Tunnels. Ho Chi Minh is like Bangalore as far as traffic is concerned - there are around 7 million two-wheelers and you can see the sea of scootys going about in the city. Therefore, we took 2 hours to reach the destination. The entire tour was amazing! Our tour guide Luna had a dark sense of humor - she kept explaining all the horrific details of the guerrilla warfare somewhat sarcastically which made everyone laugh and then stop almost immediately once they realised they shouldn't be laughing. 😅
I tried fitting into one of the tunnel entranves and succeeded - of course, have you seen me? Also because the average Vietnamese person during the war was my height and weight :p 
Sidd didn't try fitting - everyone will get jealous of how well built he is - he said. 
During the tour you can also crawl inside a 100m tunnel to experience what the soldiers went through - I thought I could do it, but I got quite claustrophobic after 40m and exited 🙈
Hats off to the entire Cu Chi community that lived inside these tunnels 😯 
Wrote a small message in the visitor's book - try and find it if you visit :) 
On the way back - our guide Luna gave us a lovely performance - she called it the Luna Live Show 😂. Sidd enjoyed the performance a lot.
Got stuck in really bad traffic on the way back and so decided to cancel all plans to go anywhere not within walking distance. 
Finished the day by trying some yum food at Quan Bui and Pasteur Street Craft Beer.
Tomorrow we go to Dalat - the adventure capital of Vietnam. 
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Drinking water is the most important thing in the world. 
Coffee: 1

steps.title: Da Lat
steps.story:
Da Lat was a lovely hilly break from all the beaches. We took a very short 35 minute flight from HCMC to Da Lat and reached our hostel - Mr. Peace Backpacker's Hostel. Check in was a little later, so we went to check out the Alpine roller coaster at the Datan La waterfall. It was a chill, fun activity to do - you get in the car and go around the mountains on the track while you control your speed. After that we rested for a bit and then went to this tourist place called the Crazy House - very aptly named - because that's what it was. It's a guesthouse with some really crazy architecture and has all sorts of scary, weird, maze-like buildings. The objective of this house was to bring people back to nature - honestly you can skip it if you're here, it's just a weird building.
We'd hired a scooty for the day and so after the crazy house we went around exploring on the bike - probably went to what felt like a 100 cafes to finally find the one that we like - realised it is very tough to find good food in Dalat. Checked out the night market here and ate some strawberries - retired early since we had to get up at 8 the next day for canyoning. 
What a fun activity - canyoning! 😯
We did it at the Datan La waterfall - the entire activity includes around 6 smaller activities that you need to complete - ziplining, swimming, hiking and the toughest of all abseiling! There were 3 cliffs from which we had to abseil, 2 of which had the water from the waterfall battering your face - every cliff I contemplated sitting out but I'm glad I didn't - the sense of achievement afterwards is unreal, even if it involves some scrapes and a slight nosebleed 😂
We did the tour through Highland Adventure Sports - do go through them since they're cheap but really good - they were sweet enough to give us yummy home cooked food afterwards and printed photo of each of us :) 
In the evening we went for a walk along the lake in Dalat, ate some amazing food at Goc Ha Tanh and crashed. Tomorrow we go to Nha Trang - another beach town - was starting to like the mountains 🏔️.

steps.title: Nha Trang
steps.story:
Late update on Nha Trang but here it is! 
We left from Da Lat in a very fancy minivan and reached Nha Trang, a beach town after a 3 hour drive. We were staying at Citadines, right next to the beach and the best part - our room had a lovely ocean view 😍
We had decided to just chill in Nha Trang before we move on to more hectic locations of Hoi An and Hanoi and that's what we did. We watched Axn on the tv (😂), I did some yoga in a very nice yoga room while Sidd hit the gym twice a day. 
We walked along the very nice beach promenade and were quite intrigued to see that every sign here was written in Russian, even the menu was in Russian - Nha Trang is almost like mini Russia in Vietnam. 
Tried multiple Banh Mis and also tried the mini pancakes here - didn't like that very much. 
In the evening, as usual, we checked out the night market which was okay-ish - we struggled to find good restaurants in Nha Trang, mostly because not much was in English, ended up ordering some butter chicken and naan from Vandana Restaurant 😂
Sidd showed off his biceps to all the Russians - as usual, the girls went crazy :p 
On our last day, after checking out, we chilled along the beach, Sidd had some 100 cups of coffee while we fought over whether censoring comedic content is correct or not. :p 
Around 4 left for the airport to go to Da Nang where we meet my parents. ❤️
Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Learning to let go of things you want to control is important. 
Coffees: 2

steps.title: Hoi An Part 1
steps.story:
We've had such a lovely time in Hoi An - not just because of the charming place that it is, but also because we've had great company! My parents and sister met us in Hoi An on the 15th evening at Nghe Resort in Hoi An. A great find again, really nice rooms, staff and breakfast 😍
The first proper day in Hoi An - we went for the basket boat ride in the coconut forest. An extremely touristy activity, but still a lot of fun - the boatmen were jovial and fun to ride along with - they kept cracking jokes, high-fiving and generally keeping things alive. It's amazing how a simple boat ride has turned so popular, with locals standing with speakers on their boats and singing APT to entertain tourists and also earn some money :p 
Taani tried her hand at fishing - albeit unsuccessful. 
After the boat ride, we tried some coconut water and a different type of coconutty fruit that they offered - which tasted a lot like the ice apples we get in Bangalore. 
After that we went to Hoi An Old town for some lunch and roamed around the picturesque streets, drinking coffee and just enjoying the vibe. 
The next day we left early for Ba Na hills - very similar to universal studios. However the highlight was this incredibly long and scary cable car! 
Saw the Golden Bridge - experienced the instagram v reality when we had to wade through huge crowds to have a look at the hands 😂
In the evening, we went to the night market in Hoi An and did the boat ride on the Thu Bon river, leaving a lantern in the water :) 
Ended the night with some relaxing foot massage.

steps.title: Hoi An Part 2
steps.story:
Every place we go to in Vietnam is pleasantly surprising us! 
After Ba Na hills, the next day, we decided to skip a trip to the city of Da Nang and visit the Marble Mountains - a 30 min drive from Hoi An. 
After some initial fights about whether to take the elevator up (and stand in a long line) or take the stairs - the stairs prevailed and we climbed up to witness magnificent caves - preserved so wonderfully! Inside the caves there were shrines of local gods and Buddha Statues with sun rays illuminating everything - it was surreal! Definitely recommend 😍
Came back and ate at a vegan restaurant which Sidd wanted to try - my dad was very disappointed with this choice (being an ardent carnivore), but ended liking his plant based chicken burger :p 
All evenings in Hoi An consisted of us going to the Old Town market and shopping, eating street food and getting foot massages 😂
The following day, we had planned to go to Cham Island, a 20 min ferry ride from Cua Dai Pier in Hoi An. The moment the ferry started we understood why it was the fastest way to go - the driver drove like a maniac, the speedboat kept bumping like a jetski with water splashing all about, so much so, the driver also had to duck. The boat was tilting to one side and Sidd and I were praying to reach safely - we looked over to parents and they were having a blast 😂 - They thought this was part of the tour and is akin to a rollercoaster 😀
Reached the island and had planned to spend a few hours on the first beach - however, the beach was not very great and so we had to rent scootys and go to the next beach - quite adventurous since we were doing tripling on one scooty and the other didn't have enough power to climb a slope :p 
Somehow we reached Bai Xep beach which was worth the trouble - completely isolated, clear waters and the best part - cold water! Everyone made attempts at snorkelling, splashed around a bit and then headed for lunch! 
A great day - ended with another shopping hour and foot massage in the evening 😂
Musings from conversations: Asked everyone what they would do if they had no fear - my sister said, she currently also has no fear - so chilling in life is what she would do :p 
Coffees: 5 :)

steps.title: Ha Noi
steps.story:
We were in Ha Noi on 21st, 23-24th and 26-27th April. 
The breaks were one day trips to places nearby. We checked into the Salute Hotel in the Old Quarter area of Hanoi. Amazing find with great location - we didn't have to take a cab anywhere. 
The first day we went to the Hang Bong road - spent quite a lot of time shopping and haggling. From there we went to the Hoan Kiem lake and ended up at Beer Street - a crazy street completely packed with small stools from all the roadside restaurants selling food and beer - there is no place to walk, you have to step over and maneuver your way through the stools to get ahead 😂
We sat in one of such restaurants and had street food - some of us tried Bia Hoi - apparently the cheapest beer in the world. 
Other days in Ha Noi consisted of a LOT of shopping - we (read my mother and I) didn't leave any market - we even ended up at the wholesale market here (Ninh Heip) where no tourist goes to get the best deals. Tips for anyone who is a shopping fanatic - go to Ninh Heip if you can (it's quite far from any main tourist places), don't shop at any other market - wait for the night market that gets set up every weekend near the Hoan Kiem lake and do all your shopping there. 
Sidd's patience was tested quite a bit during the shopping sprees where he accompanied us. 😂
One night we went to watch the water puppet show at Thang Long Theatre - it's a nice show, and we went since it was very highly recommended, though honestly if you don't have a lot of time, it's quite skippable. 
Went to the Note Cafe - a cafe smothered with notes from whoever passes by. It's crazy how many notes there are, they're even in the bathroom! Read a lot of them - some of them were quite hilarious, some had phone numbers asking people who were reading to drop a message - my sister might become pen pals with some of them :p 
We also left a little something for other wanderers to read - try to find it if you're here. :) 
We of course tried the train street, after dodging some cafe mafias, watched the train go by an inch away from where we sat - even kept a beer cap on the rails for the train to flatten it - it's now for keeps :) 
Hanoi gives you all the city feels - people are transactional, everyone is in a hurry, you finally see some potholes and garbage lying around - but the place has its own charm with its umpteen cafes selling egg coffees and lava cakes. While we liked Hoi An better, Ha noi is a fun city to visit as well. 
Updates from our day trips to Ninh Binh and Bai Tu Long in the subsequent blogs :p

steps.title: Ninh Binh (Day Trip from Hanoi)
steps.story:
Ninh Binh is a small town around 2 hours away from Ha Noi - it used to be Vietnam's capital in the 10th century. We left early on 22nd from Ha Noi to go to Ninh Binh with our very lively and energetic driver for the day - Mr. Duc (I'm sure that's not the spelling, but that's how you pronounce it). 
He played patriotic Vietnamese songs for us (with video) the entire way and sang and danced along it as well :p 
Our first stop was the Hoa Lu temple -  Vietnam is a largely atheist country, and so they worship a lot of their ancestors and kings. The Hoa Lu temple was also dedicated to some of these kings - that's what my parents told us - since Sidd, my sister and I rented bicycles and went riding around the countryside behind the temple 🙈. The temple complex seemed very pretty though. 
Even though we wanted our next stop to be the Trang An boat ride, our driver Mr. Duc had other plans for us. He insisted that we eat first (at 11:30 am) since that was how he had planned the day :p 
So we ate again at his recommended restaurant and then went on to Trang An - a scenic boat ride - that is the only must do thing in Ninh Binh according to us. 
There are 4 routes that you can take with 3 of them lasting 3-3.5 hours and 1 lasting around 2 hours. We took the shortest one, but we weren't disappointed. The boat ride is beautiful, they take you under caves and stop at spiritual sites in the middle of the water - we absolutely loved it. Please witness Sidd attempting a solo photoshoot while we were all busy sightseeing :p 
By the end of it we were quite tired - we were supposed to go to the Mua Cave after this, but decided to go back to Ha Noi and rest for a bit. 
Nights of course consisted of some window shopping and good food at a rooftop restaurant. 
A very good day, very well spent!

steps.title: Bai Tu Long Cruise
steps.story:
The trip to Bai Tu Long Bay (Bai Tu Long meaning baby dragon) started early in the morning at 7. We were booked with Swan Cruises who came to pick us up in a nice van - we had to drive for 2 hours to reach Ha Long City, from where we could board the boat. 
Mr. Tommy was our tour guide for the day who was quite funny and unburdened a lot of his problems on us during the journey - he complained hilariously about politics, the government, traffic, corruption, housing, floods - basically everything wrong with Vietnam. Felt like a living room conversation between 4 middle aged uncles in India 😂 
We finally reached Ha Long City, a city developed on reclaimed land especially for tourism but which didn't quite reach its potential and so you can see a lot of under-construction buildings that people left midway after investments ran dry. 
We got on our cruise from the Ha Long City port and started sailing for Bai Tu Long. The cruise was a large wooden boat, with really wooden nice interiors and fancy rooms. We were then served a filling 5 course meal after which we slept while the boat cruised towards Bai Tu Long - ofcourse! :) 
Woke up to do the first activity of the day - Kayaking and swimming. Taani (my sister), the fifth wheel on this trip was made to kayak with a stranger while Sidd, me and mom, dad were together on 2 Kayaks. We were to Kayak from our boat to a nearby beach - Sidd and I and Taani managed to reach the beach only to see my parents had turned around midway, back to the boat. Quite justified I think - they were here to relax and we were forcing them into strenuous activities. 😂
Went back to the boat where some more activities were planned - the crew organised a cooking class where they taught us how to make Vietnamese spring rolls - Taani and my mom participated. After dinner, some people tried their hand at squid fishing and others did karaoke. My dad - who'd by now become best friends with the cruise manager sang "Jab Koi Baat Bigad Jaye" with the cruise manager - (who did very well at singing a hindi song) - serenading my mom, don't think the cruise manager knew what the song meant 😂
Next morning - we woke up early to go to a cave. We hiked up to the entrance and were amazed to see the inside - it was too pretty! Spent some time there and then went back - they served us an early lunch and dropped us back to Ha Long from where we rode back to Hanoi. 
A nice night spent amidst the waters - it's a fun activity to do with a large crowd - could maybe skip it if you're a small group. 

Musings from our conversations: My dad has suggested to change my sister's name to Bai Tu Long i.e., baby dragon - we all agree - considering the traits match :p

steps.title: Ha Giang Loop 3D2N
steps.story:
Ha Giang Loop was literally a pain in the ass - but not figuratively :p 
Apart from the sore bums - we loved the entire experience, even though the landscape reminded us of our trips to Himachal, there were many things the loop had which we hadn't experienced before! 
For those who don't know - Ha Giang Loop is a 3 day 2 nights tour where you ride all day on a scooty to some of the remotest places in Vietnam and stop along the way to see viewpoints and do some activities. 

Day 1 

We had taken a night bus from Hanoi and reached Ha Giang city at around 4 am, slept for 4 hours and were up at 8 to leave. 
Our group consisted of 6 people - both of us, a Portugese couple - Juan and Quita and another couple - Antonio from Brazil and Augustina from Uruguay. Our group leader was interestingly named Kiss (:p), he was also Sidd's rider which Sidd thoroughly enjoyed - always being ahead of all the scootys :p 
The first day we rode up to some amazing views, started getting to know our group better - realised what a privilege we have knowing English as almost our first language, apparently it's a big deal for others. We visited this lovely village in a valley which largely grew corn - so corn was all that was there as far as the eye could see. Kiss took us to one of the houses in the village, to show us how the Humong people (natives of this village) live - while it must have been a great experience for the Europeans seeing cattle, fodder and huts, for us it wasn't a big deal - we see plenty of cows at home :p 
But the owners of the house were really sweet, they didn't know any english but they sat down with us and tried to talk, also made us take shots of their local liquor which they call "Happy Water" :p 
Happy water is a big deal here, everyone has a lot of it and if someone offers to have it with you, you have to have it - it's rude to refuse! 
We finished our day and reached the first destination - a quaint homestay in Don Vang village. Had some amazing dinner, were forced to drink shots of Happy water with the riders and owner of the homestay and while everyone else partied and sang karaoke - Sidd and I went to sleep at 9 pm 😂. 

Day 2 

Started out at 9 am. By now we'd all become friends with the riders and the people in our group - so the conversations were fun, Kiss shared that he'd been working for 36 days non-stop and riding and talking to tourists is how he learnt english! 
Our first stop of the day was this river which led to a cave - you had to sit on a bamboo raft to reach the cave. Once we reached the cave entrance we all jumped into the water and swam - the water was extremely cold but a lot of fun! Went into the cave which was majestic and super quiet - a definite highlight of the day :') 
The swim made us forget our bum pain and everyone was in an even better mood after it - the riders blasted music on speakers on their scootys, Sidd connected his phone and played rap music! My scooty rider was a shy guy so sadly I didn't get any music, but I enjoyed my thoughts while riding through the mountains - gave me sometime to plot my plans on how to annoy Sidd next :) 
Next stop was Ma Pi Leng pass and the view of an emerald river cutting across the canyon between 2 mountains was breathtaking! You could see China at a distance, Airtel even sent me a message welcoming me to China 😂
Sidd didn't want to click any romantic pictures with me - he didn't want the girls who were going crazy to know that we were together. 
From there we had an option to either walk up a mountain or ride upto the China border - I wanted to go to the border but Sidd wanted to walk and so he prevailed with his sophisticated diplomacy skills - which basically consisted of telling people not to listen to me "She's just lazy to walk", he said 😂
I'm glad we did the walk though - it's a UNESCO heritage site and there we learnt that the entire road connecting Ha Giang city of these remote villages were made by the local people and not by the government. They made it over 5 years for a better life and resources but just cutting the mountains themselves without any machinery!! Which is why the road is called the Happiness road :) 
Ended the day at another lovely homestay and tried Hotpot for the first time. To not be such party poopers all the time - we did not sleep at 9 - instead we ended up doing karaoke and teaching Tunak Tunak Tun Tarara steps our group as well as some Irish riders who were there at the hotel 😂. I wish we had a video - Sidd looked absolutely amazing singing punjabi lyrics and doing bhangra. We also learnt the Irish jig and some Brazilian funk music. It was a lovely night with lots of culture intermingling - even the hosts joined in to sing some Vietnamese songs! 

Day 3

Started at 9 am again - we were riding back to Ha Giang City on day 3. On the way we stopped at another village and visited a very sweet lady's house who showed us how the Humong people make clothes from Hemp plants, even made us try some one the steps. She was quite funny as well - she told us that all clothes are made by women while her husband drinks "happy water everyday with his best friend" 😂. Then she told us the story of how she met her husband on Facebook and ran away with him. Apparently in their village, the husband has to pay dowry to buy the bride from her parents - she told us she was very expensive:p 
The best story of all though was how she decided to make the practice of making hemp clothes popular outside of her village and so she learnt english on Duolingo and started a FB and Instagram page to sell the products that she made. She was so proud of herself, it was extremely cute and inspirational 😍 
From there we stopped at multiple places with lovely views or just to rest! Reached Ha Giang at 4 pm and immediately took a bus back to Hanoi. 
We'll go to Laos next! More from there! 

Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Patriotism is a personal choice - should not be forced upon somebody. 

Coffees: 2

steps.title: Vientiane
steps.story:
Reached Laos - went through a tedious immigration process at Vientiane Airport which is ironically named Wattay airport :p 
Didn't do much here except eat at the night market. 
The next day we took a bullet train to Vang Vieng - the bullet train is made by China. A lot of things in Laos are made by China, most signs are also in Chinese. Talk about world dominance 😀
Updates from Vang Vieng in the next blog!

steps.title: Vang Vieng
steps.story:
Vang Vieng is a weird sleepy village - some definite natural wonders that you'll enjoy but apart from that not much to do. There are hardly any restaurants as well + you can walk the entire village 😀 
We reached around 11 and were welcomed by burning heat and so we decided to visit the famous blue lagoons here. We decided to go to the most recommended blue lagoon 4 and it did not disappoint 😍 
The water is gorgeous nestled amidst the mountains. There's a zip line and other jumps that you can do. I tried the zip line and thoroughly enjoyed it - Sidd kept jumping from this one platform and forced me to jump too. There were very few people there and everyone was cheering the other on to try the jumps! It was quite wholesome and nice. After that we went to visit the Jang Cave - the biggest one we've visited so far! It was lit up and very pretty inside - but once you've been in a cave for 2 min, you don't really know what to do after that :p Maybe we're just saturated with caves. We watched the hot air balloons at sunset from our hotel room and then had dinner at one of the few decent restaurants here and called it a night. 
The next day, the sun scared us so we didn't step out in the mornings - went out in the evening for kayaking along the Nam Song river. Laoations like to party a lot! Vang Vieng has this culture of small bars set up on the river, where all locals gather and swim and drink and play trippy music. We passed all these bars while kayaking and watched everyone partying hard :p 
Apparently this town used to be much more of a party town as compared to now, however, after some unfortunate deaths due to overdosed restricted Vang Vieng's hedonistic activities. 
Day 3 - It rained! The weather was finally good so we decided to do a trek - once we reached there, travelling through horrible muddy roads of Laos - people there told us the trek is very slippery and not worth it in this weather and so we decided to check out Lagoon 1. Lagoon 1 was horrible, too crowded and the water did not look good - so we left and went to Lagoon 2. Lagoon 2 was sooo much fun! A lot more people as compared to Lagoon 4 but the vibe was a lot of fun. There was music playing, the locals and tourists were all having fun. There was really high jump into the water that was "the" thing to do here. It became a test of your bravery after a point :p 
Sidd's first jump required 4 attempts and there's a video of mine requiring "750 attempts" 😂
There were some people who stood there for hours but couldn't jump - after a point everyone there started cheering for people who couldn't jump 🥺 - it was very cute and wholesome :') 
From here we move to Luang Prabang - hopefully there will be better places to eat there. 

Coffees: 6

steps.title: Luang Prabang
steps.story:
After a short train ride from Vang Vieng, we reached Luang Prabang. Luang Prabang is a quaint town, designated as a UNESCO world heritage site for having preserved its colonial architecture. However, when we reached it was scorching hot and we had to endure a short but painful mini-van ride into the main town. After a deadly 5 min walk, we finally reached our guest house - Museum Inn, Luang Prabang. A very nice place - clean rooms and a filling breakfast in the mornings! 
Loas sun in May is unbearable. We were a little bummed since we weren't able to enjoy the town as much as we would've had we come in better weather. We resorted to only going out in the early mornings and late evenings - also our restaurant selections depended on whether there was AC or not 😂
Ended up eating at one place thrice - Phan Souk Restaurant - go there if you're interested in really cheap yet good local food. 
The first day, we roamed around the town - it is definitely very pretty and quite similar to Hoi An. The sunsets in Laos are one of the most beautiful I've ever seen and we caught a lovely one while walking along the Mae Kong river! Ate at Tamarind - a recommendation by our guest house. The food was great, but the best part was their menu which explained local cuisine in great detail and even had a little section about the owners! I learnt that sticky rice is a specific type of rice and not a method of preparation 😯
The next day, we woke up early to go to the Kuang Si waterfall - which in all its glory (i.e, in the winter) is something out of a fairytale, however in the summer, it relatively has less water. We were prepared for not having an otherworldly experience, however the waterfall was extremely pretty even with not as much water. Before we went to the waterfall, we went through a bear sanctuary and saw some cute little black bears :') 
Ran into chinese tourists we met on the train as well - for some weird reason, all the Chinese aunties kept wanting to click a picture with us, we didn't understand why because of the language barrier - Sidd thinks it's because we probably look like a different species to them. Felt like quite the celebrity 😎
Back to the waterfall - while the waterfall is beautiful as it falls over limestone rocks, the best were the turquoise blue pools that were created for us to swim in! The water was cold and clean - you had to continuously keep moving though otherwise the fish would nip at your skin. Sidd wore his neon orange shorts which he proudly acquired in the night markets of Vietnam - I think it was his orange shorts that prompted the Chinese people to want a picture with us :) 
After a painful ride back on the non-roads of Laos we came back and stayed indoors for the afternoon - went out in the evening and visited one of the pretty cafes and a nearby Wat. 
The next morning, we woke up at 5 am!! A big feat for us in my opinion. This very early morning was to watch the Alms giving ceremony - where the monks from all the Wats go around the town and the residents offer them food as an act of service/devotion. After that we trekked up Mount Phousi to see the view from up there - the people here believe that Mount Phousi is the same hill that Hanuman got for Lakshman with the Sanjeevani in Ramayan. The view was certainly divine from up there. 
Came back down and went back home through the morning market, wading through a sea of food and unknown smells 😅
Tomorrow we shall cross the border back to Thailand - to visit the North of Thailand. 

Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Low expectations make way for pleasant surprises :) 

Coffees: 3 :)

steps.title: Chiang Rai
steps.story:
Our trip from Luang Prabang to Chiang Khong and then Chiang Rai has been the weirdest and most adventurous one till date! 
We first took a 2 hour train from LP to Nateuy - this train wasn't the fancy bullet one, it was the slow train with hard seats and I was lucky enough to be seated with some very loud chinese uncles. Just when I thought that was irritating - we had a 5 hour road trip ahead to Huay Xai where we would cross our border. Remember the deadly minivan ride I mentioned in my earlier blog? Imagine that for 5 hours with a driver who I'm convinced used to be a F1 driver! 😂 Add hilly non-existent roads to the mix and you've got some nauseated  passengers :). I was honestly enjoying my ride after some time while Sidd was quite uncomfortable - I tried to play 20 questions but he did not like my distraction techniques :( 
Finally reached Huay Xai around 7pm and went to the border crossing - which has to be the shadiest border crossing we've ever done. There was no one there except for the two of us - the immigration officer was in his home clothes and asked us to pay him money to exit the country! 
They then asked us for more money to help us cross the friendship bridge - a distance of 700m. At this eerie crossing - while we waited for the bus, some people sat around a table drinking beer and chilling 😂 
Thankfully we were joined by some loud and drunk locals (don't know if lao or thai) who were crossing the border as well. After 20 min, our bus driver came to take us to the other side - he was one of the gentlemen from the beer drinking table :p 
The town on the other side of the border was Chiang Khong. The Thai immigration officer was in his running clothes and least interested in whether we were legitimate tourists or fugitives - he just wanted to go for his run 😅
We were taking this particular journey on the fly, like true backpackers we didn't know where we were going to stay the night and so hadn't booked any place. We were hoping we could reach Chiang Rai the same day, if we caught a late night bus but once we reached Chiang Khong we realised there are no buses at that time of the day. We quickly booked a nearby B&B. The owner saw us and asked if we were Kashmiri. He went on to say "Not good - fighting going on" 😔
I think it was his way of sharing his opinion on war. 
After a 7-11 meal, we crashed like a log. The next morning, we went out in search of buses to Chiang Rai and the only one we could find was a red local chariot (see pics for reference). It was a typical local bus, which felt like it would disintegrate any moment. At one point Sidd said the only thing left is for an animal to walk in and then it would be the complete experience 😂
I really enjoyed my bus ride though, the ride was scenic, the weather was good, wind was blowing in my face - and the violent shaking of the bus put me in a nice slumber 😊
Reached Chiang Rai, checked into our hostel and left to see the White Temple. One of the prettiest temples I've seen in Thailand. In the evening we visited the night market which was sooo lively, we tried so much food and walked around - but the best part was the town square kind of area where a local artist was singing and everyone around was just dancing! It was such a happy, wholesome atmosphere and quite contagious as well. I tried to get Sidd to dance - by now you can guess what he said - "Girls will go crazy!" 🙄. Still, I managed to get some hipshakes out of him. 
Tomorrow and day after we travel again to reach Pai. More later! 

Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: Inconveniences can easily become adventures if you want them to :) 

Coffees: 0

steps.title: Pai
steps.story:
Pai is definitely in the top 5 places we've visited on this trip! 
We left at 10 am from Chiang Mai in a minivan again (this time we got good seats). In the 24 hours preceding this ride, all Sidd could talk about was the "treacherous road" that we had to ride to Pai. Apparently there are 762 hairpin bends on the drive to Pai, and roads are winding - so it could be difficult for people who get motion sickness. However, we were lucky to get a good drive so we didn't feel anything at all - in fact, I thought this was one of the most scenic drives we've done this trip. The weather was fantastic, the roads were lined with trees on both sides and you had beautiful green mountain views all through the ride :') 
We reached, checked into a very nice resort - The Quarter, had lunch but couldn't do much since it was very hot. In the evening though, the weather turned and it rained and we were blessed with similar weather throughout our stay! 😍
The rain made all the difference, we went out to the main walking street which was a great vibe. There were rows of cute cafes, yummy street food and so many great bars. We sat at a quant cafe, had ginger tea and cookies, tried home made lasagna, sat at a bar and watched people - still ended the night at 9:30 pm 🤣
Watched Da Vinci Code and slept. 
The next day, we drove to Bamboo Bridge - a touristy spot - which is a 800m walk on a bamboo bridge with scenic views. 
Loved the drive, got stuck in the rain again, took shelter in a shed like a bollywood movie, however didn't talk about anything romantic - Sidd talked to me about his love for cycles :) 
The Bamboo Bridge was decent, would've been better if the rice fields were in full bloom. Nevertheless, we enjoyed the weather and the views. Sidd was very excited to click a picture with the bamboo heart :p 
Had tea at Jaey Cafe with lazy cats. Came back and repeated our evening ritual of street food and people watching. 
The next day, we lazed around at our resort, swam and went to the Pai Canyon in the evening to see the sunset. Ended up seeing the sunset on the scooty on the way (🙈) but still enjoyed the Canyon.
The next day, didn't do much - rode to a nice view point, drove around town and watched Don 😂
For our rides back to Chiang Mai, Sidd and I decided to part ways. Sidd drove a scooty back and I came in the minivan. From what I hear, his ride was epic. :) 
More on Chiang Mai later. 

Musings from Sidd and Shreya's Conversations: Good weather makes everything so much better 🫠

Coffees: 2

steps.title: Chiang Mai
steps.story:
Chiang Mai has been rainy but yet a lot of fun. We didn't spend a lot of time in the city though - ended up doing all the touristy things around the city. 
The day we reached we didn't do anything apart from visiting the night markets here as usual. 
The next day we'd booked a tour to visit the Sticky waterfalls and fulfill Sidd's lifelong wish to see a baby elephant.
The sticky waterfalls were a lot of fun - it's called sticky because the rocks over which the water flows have excessive calcium carbonate deposits because of which you can climb up the waterfall like you're climbing stairs - 0 slipperiness, max grip.  🌝
Next we drove to the elephant sanctuary where we would get to hang out with elephants. They made us wear special kaftan tshirts (known as Karen clothing) - which resembles the kind of clothing that the Mahauts wear - this is so that the elephants recognise as familiar beings and do not kick us. Finally the elephants came and they were so cuteee! Especially the two babies - Rambo and Dumbo. We fed them bananas and watched them frolick around in the rain. Sidd was obsessed with Dumbo (coincidence? 😂) and followed him around - Dumbo reciprocated the love by giving us a show of him splashing in the pool and then making his own pool in the mud :p 
We loved the entire experience. If you visit, make sure you choose a company that does not offer riding - that's actually quite brutal for the elephants and is considered unethical. 
The next day we went to the Doi Inthanon National Park, one hour away from Chiang Mai, and we are so glad we went. It was the best activity we did in Chiang Mai. 
Started early around 7 am to drive to the national park. It was a rainy day and the drive was quite scenic. Inside the National Park we went to the highest point in Thailand and the trail to it was through a jungle and it was beautiful. From there we visited the pagaodas made to pay respect to the King and Queen of Thailand - I keep repeating myself but everywhere we went the views were just breathtaking. The mountains were green and forest covered with clouds floating over them, the weather was cool - it was a beautiful day! From there we had lunch and then explored the forests inside the National Park through a 2 hour trek. Walked through lovely jungle trails, visited 3 waterfalls, saw a green snake - best part was walking the entire trek alongside an 85 year old uncle from Germany! He did the entire tour with us and walked at our place throughout - kudos to his fitness. ❤️
Came back and had a blast at dinner with our friends from Mumbai who're also travelling in Thailand. 
Chiang Mai was a great end to a rollercoaster of a trip. Tomorrow we fly back to India and finish this 4 month long journey we set out on. 
We shall share one more parting blog - so there's still more later! 

Musings from Sidd and Shreya's conversations: German uncle is old age goals! 

Coffees: 2

steps.title: Bombay - Fin 🏠
steps.story:
What felt like a preposterous idea a year back has finally come to an end. I'm writing this as I sit at the airport in Bangkok, waiting for our flight back to Bombay (and the accompanying reality). This 100-day adventure has been truly special, starting from the point where I had to convince Shreya to go for it. And now, after 75,694 buses, trains, flights, and ferries—or at least what felt like that many—we are returning to India (a few kgs heavier and infinitely richer in experiences).

We like to think of ourselves as travelers rather than tourists, collecting moments and memories rather than souvenirs (coming back home empty-handed, this is my excuse). As we prepare to return to normal life and face the Monday blues, I'm ending this note forever grateful for the privilege to embark on this journey and for having someone who turns every challenge into an adventure worth sharing.

Our favourite places from the entire journey: 

- Ubud, Bali, Indonesia 🇮🇩
- Singapore 🇸🇬
- Georgetown, Penang, Malaysia 🇲🇾
- Krabi, Thailand 🇹🇭
- Koh Tao, Thailand 🇹🇭 ⭐
- Koh Rong, Cambodia 🇰🇭
- Hoi An, Vietnam 🇻🇳 ⭐
- Luang Prabang, Laos 🇱🇦
- Chiang Mai, Thailand 🇹🇭
- Pai, Thailand 🇹🇭 ⭐
